```{python}
#| tags: [setup]
import sys, os, re, itertools, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import doe_report as D
import tables as T          # complex tables: merged cells, footnotes (T.<builder>(...).show())
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import scipy.stats as sstat
import statsmodels.api as sm
from amab_process import adequacy as ad

DOC = "PCR-007"
UO = "cex"
UO_TITLE = "Cation Exchange Chromatography (Step 7)"

# --- names, units, thresholds --------------------------------------------------------------
uo = CFG.unit_op(UO)
FAC = D.rsm_factors(UO)
LET = D.factor_letters(UO)
PN = {p.key: p.name for p in uo.parameters}
_lc = lambda s: re.sub(r"(^|/)([A-Z])(?=[a-z])", lambda m: m.group(1) + m.group(2).lower(), s)   # "load/wash conductivity"
pn = {k: _lc(v) for k, v in PN.items()}
UNIT = {p.key: re.sub(r"\s*\(.*\)$", "", p.unit) for p in uo.parameters}
num, crit = T.num, T.crit
pq = lambda p: "p < 0.001" if p < 0.001 else f"p = {p:.3f}"
fm = lambda v, nd=2: T._minus(f"{v:.{nd}f}")          # a value that can be negative, with a true minus
ALPHA = float(THRESHOLDS["effect_alpha"])
RALPHA = float(THRESHOLDS["residual_alpha"])
LOFA = float(THRESHOLDS["lof_alpha"])
GAPMAX = float(THRESHOLDS["max_r2_minus_pred_r2"])
COOKF = float(THRESHOLDS["cook_factor"])
COOKQ = float(THRESHOLDS["cook_f_quantile"])
PI_PCT = int(round(100 * D.PI_LEVEL))
PI_UP = 100 - (100 - PI_PCT) / 2
CI_PCT = int(round(100 * float(CFG.raw()["analytics"]["sdm"]["offset_ci"])))
VB_PCT = int(round(100 * D.VERIFICATION_BOUND))
NMC = int(V["n_monte_carlo"])
SCALE_L = int(V["commercial_scale_l"])
MC_SEED, PAR_N, PAR_GRID = D.PAR_SEED, D.PAR_MC_N, D.PAR_GRID
NOR_DIV = D.NOR_SD_DIVISOR


def prng(f, which="nor"):
    """A range of a parameter in prose: '18–32 g/L resin', 'pH 5.85–6.15'."""
    p = uo.param(f)
    lo, hi = {"nor": p.nor, "range": p.prange}[which]
    return f"pH {lo:g}–{hi:g}" if UNIT[f] == "pH" else f"{lo:g}–{hi:g} {UNIT[f]}"


def pset(f, v):
    """A setting of a parameter in prose: '40 g/L resin', 'pH 6.2'."""
    return f"pH {v:g}" if UNIT[f] == "pH" else f"{v:g} {UNIT[f]}"


def tname(t):
    """A model term in words."""
    if ":" in t:
        a, b = t.split(":")
        return f"{pn[a]} × {pn[b]}"
    if t.endswith("^2"):
        return pn[t[:-2]] + "²"
    return pn[t]


def corner(settings, facs=None):
    """A combination of settings in prose: 'protein load 40 g/L resin, ..., elution buffer pH 6.2'."""
    return join_and([f"{pn[f]} {float(settings[f]):g}" if UNIT[f] == "pH" else f"{pn[f]} {pset(f, float(settings[f]))}"
                     for f in (facs or FAC)])


# --- chronology (study_chronology.csv) ------------------------------------------------------
CHR = csv("study_chronology.csv").set_index("id")
win = lambda s: f"{CHR.loc[s, 'start']} to {CHR.loc[s, 'end']}"
CHAR_STUDIES = ["S-CEX-SDM", "S-CEX-SCR", "S-CEX-RSM", "S-CEX-UNI", "S-CEX-FRC"]
assert CHR.loc["S-CEX-SDM", "end"] < CHR.loc["S-CEX-SCR", "start"]          # qualification first
assert CHR.loc["S-CEX-SCR", "end"] < CHR.loc["S-CEX-RSM", "start"]          # screening before RSM
assert CHR.loc["S-CEX-RSM", "start"] <= CHR.loc["S-CEX-UNI", "start"] and CHR.loc["S-CEX-UNI", "end"] <= CHR.loc["S-CEX-RSM", "end"]
CHAR_START = min(CHR.loc[s, "start"] for s in CHAR_STUDIES)
CHAR_END = max(CHR.loc[s, "end"] for s in CHAR_STUDIES)
assert CHAR_END < REV1["effective"]
PLAN_V1 = rev1_date("PCP-007")
assert PLAN_V1 < CHR.loc["S-CEX-SDM", "start"]
assert INV["closed"] < CHR.loc["S-CEX-VER", "start"] and CHR.loc["S-CEX-VER", "end"] <= EFFECTIVE_DATE
assert INV["closed"] < CHR.loc["S-VI-WC", "start"] and CHR.loc["S-VI-WC", "end"] <= EFFECTIVE_DATE
EQ = csv("dev_equipment.csv").set_index("id").loc["EQ-CHR-118"]
assert CHR.loc["S-CEX-RSM", "equipment"] == "EQ-CHR-118" and CHR.loc["S-CEX-RSM", "end"] < EQ["cal_due"]
assert all(pd.isna(CHR.loc[s, "equipment"]) for s in CHAR_STUDIES if s != "S-CEX-RSM")
assert AMD["date"] > CHR.loc["S-CEX-SCR", "end"] and CHR.loc["S-CEX-RSM", "start"] < AMD["date"] < CHR.loc["S-CEX-RSM", "end"]
assert CHR.loc["S-CEX-UNI", "end"] < AMD["date"] or CHR.loc["S-CEX-UNI", "start"] < AMD["date"]
CA3_DATE = re.search(r"adopted on (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})", str(CAPA2.set_index("id").loc["CA3", "status"])).group(1)
assert CA3_DATE < INV["closed"]

# --- parameters and classes -----------------------------------------------------------------
RP = report_params(UO)
N_PAR = len(RP)
N_MV = int((RP["Study"] == "multivariate").sum())
N_UNI = int((RP["Study"] == "univariate").sum())
N_WC = int((RP["Class"] == "WC-CPP").sum())
N_CPP = int((RP["Class"] == "CPP").sum())
N_GPP = int((RP["Class"] == "GPP").sum())
N_KPP = int((RP["Class"] == "KPP").sum())
assert N_WC + N_CPP + N_GPP + N_KPP == N_PAR and N_CPP == 0 and N_KPP == 0 and N_GPP == 1
UNI_KEY = [p.key for p in uo.parameters if p.study == "univariate"]
assert UNI_KEY == ["flow"] and set(FAC) == {p.key for p in uo.parameters if p.study == "multivariate"}
assert all(T.nor_change(p) is None for p in uo.parameters)          # no NOR or set-point moved at this step
assert all(p.setpoint == p.setpoint_characterized for p in uo.parameters)
assert all(p.setpoint == (p.prange[0] + p.prange[1]) / 2 for p in uo.parameters)   # set-point = design centre
assert all(p.prange[0] < p.nor[0] and p.nor[1] < p.prange[1] for p in uo.parameters)
CLS = {p.key: p.classification for p in uo.parameters}
N_PD = len(PLAN_DISCREPANCIES.get(DOC, []))
assert N_PD == 12 and [d["id"] for d in PLAN_DISCREPANCIES[DOC]] == [f"PD-007-{i:02d}" for i in range(1, 13)]
assert all(CLS[f] == "WC-CPP" for f in FAC) and CLS["flow"] == "GPP"
SP = {p.key: float(p.setpoint) for p in uo.parameters}
SP4 = {f: SP[f] for f in FAC}
PR = {p.key: tuple(p.prange) for p in uo.parameters}
NORR = {p.key: tuple(p.nor) for p in uo.parameters}
MARG = {f: NORR[f][0] - PR[f][0] for f in FAC}
assert all(abs((NORR[f][0] - PR[f][0]) - (PR[f][1] - NORR[f][1])) < 1e-9 for f in FAC)

# --- designs ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCR = csv("doe_cex_screening.csv")
RSM = csv("doe_cex_rsm.csv")
N_SCR, N_RSM = doe_runs(UO, "screening"), doe_runs(UO, "rsm")
NC_SCR, NC_RSM = doe_centre_points(UO, "screening"), doe_centre_points(UO, "rsm")
NF_SCR = int((SCR.run_type == "factorial").sum())
NF_RSM = int((RSM.run_type == "factorial").sum())
NA_RSM = int((RSM.run_type == "axial").sum())
assert NF_SCR == 2 ** len(FAC) and NF_RSM == 2 ** len(FAC) and NA_RSM == 2 * len(FAC)
CO_SCR = sorted(int(x) for x in SCR[SCR.run_type == "center"]["run_order"])
CO_RSM = sorted(int(x) for x in RSM[RSM.run_type == "center"]["run_order"])
N_CAND = len(ad.hierarchical_subsets(FAC))
N_FULL = len(ad.full_terms(FAC))           # terms besides the intercept
assert not D.has_augmentation(UO)
assert D.setting_corrections(UO, "rsm") == [] and D.setting_corrections(UO, "screening") == []
# what the record holds (PCP-007 §5.4 sampled the load of every run)
assert not any(c.startswith(("dna_", "lpa_")) or "load_" in c for c in SCR.columns)
assert "dna_pool_pg_mg" in RSM.columns and "lpa_pool_ppm" in RSM.columns
assert not any(("aggregate" in c or "hcp" in c) and "load" in c for c in RSM.columns)
FRAG_M = D.fragment_responses(UO, "rsm")
assert FRAG_M == ["lmw_sec_pct", "lmw_cesds_pct"] and D.fragment_responses(UO, "screening") == ["lmw_sec_pct"]

# --- criteria -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
RESPC = ["aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg", "lmw_cesds_pct"]
ACC = {r: D.effective_acceptance(UO, r) for r in RESPC}
IAC = D.iac_table(UO).set_index("response")
C_AGG, C_HCP, C_FRAG = (num(ACC[r][1]) for r in RESPC)
C_HCP_AP = num(IAC.loc["hcp_out_ng_mg", "iac_high_apriori"])
assert bool(IAC.loc["hcp_out_ng_mg", "widened"]) and not bool(IAC.loc["hcp_out_ng_mg", "tightened"])
assert bool(IAC.loc["aggregate_out_pct", "tightened"]) and not bool(IAC.loc["aggregate_out_pct", "widened"])
assert not bool(IAC.loc["lmw_cesds_pct", "tightened"]) and IAC.loc["lmw_cesds_pct", "basis"] == "drug substance"
assert float(IAC.loc["aggregate_out_pct", "downstream_fold"]) == 1.0 and float(IAC.loc["lmw_cesds_pct", "downstream_added"]) == 0.0
C_AGG_AP = num(IAC.loc["aggregate_out_pct", "iac_high_apriori"])
assert float(IAC.loc["aggregate_out_pct", "iac_high_apriori"]) == float(CQA_DS_AGG := csv("cqa_register.csv").set_index("key").loc["aggregates_hmw", "acc_high"])
# the UF/DF allowance: the one-sided single-run bound of the aggregate rise across UF/DF (S-UFDF-UNI2, offset applied)
VUF = D.iac_verification("ufdf").set_index("cqa").loc["aggregates_hmw"]
UFDF_ADD = float(IAC.loc["aggregate_out_pct", "downstream_added"])
assert abs(float(VUF["predicted_nor_bound95"]) - UFDF_ADD) < 1e-3 and not bool(VUF["met"]) and float(VUF["assumed"]) == 0.0
assert abs(float(CQA_DS_AGG) - UFDF_ADD - ACC["aggregate_out_pct"][1]) < 1e-9
HCP_DSF = float(IAC.loc["hcp_out_ng_mg", "downstream_fold"])
R1 = D.rev1_criteria(UO).set_index("response")
R1_AGG, R1_HCP = num(R1.loc["aggregate_out_pct", "high"]), num(R1.loc["hcp_out_ng_mg", "high"])
R1_MAG, R1_MHCP = num(R1.loc["aggregate_out_pct", "margin"], 1), num(R1.loc["hcp_out_ng_mg", "margin"], 1)
CQA = csv("cqa_register.csv").set_index("key")
IAC_ALL = D.iac_table()
_ia = lambda sk, resp: IAC_ALL[(IAC_ALL.step_key == sk) & (IAC_ALL.response == resp)].iloc[0]
UP_BRX, UP_VI = _ia("bioreactor", "aggregates_hmw"), _ia("viral_inactivation", "aggregate_out_pct")
UP_PA_HCP, UP_PA_LPA = _ia("protein_a", "pool_hcp_ng_mg"), _ia("protein_a", "leached_protein_a_ppm")
UP_PA_FRAG, UP_VI_FRAG = _ia("protein_a", "lmw_cesds_pct"), _ia("viral_inactivation", "lmw_cesds_pct")
UP_AEX_HCP = _ia("aex", "hcp_out_ng_mg")
assert bool(UP_BRX["tightened"]) and bool(UP_VI["tightened"]) and bool(UP_BRX["widened"]) and not bool(UP_VI["widened"])

# --- selected response-surface models -------------------------------------------------------
RS = ["aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg", "lmw_cesds_pct", "step_yield"]
FIT = {r: D.fit(UO, "rsm", r) for r in RS}
RI = {r: D.residual_influence(UO, r) for r in RS}
FA, FH, FF, FY = (FIT[r] for r in RS)
assert FA["status"] == "selected" and FA["transform"] == "log"
assert FH["status"] == "selected" and FH["transform"] == "log"
assert FF["status"] == "none" and FF["transform"] is None and not FF["exact"]
assert FF["gap"] > GAPMAX and FF["p_lof"] >= LOFA and FF["p"] < ALPHA
assert FY["status"] == "selected" and FY["transform"] is None
for r in ("aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg"):
    assert FIT[r]["p"] < ALPHA and FIT[r]["p_lof"] >= LOFA and FIT[r]["gap"] <= GAPMAX
    assert FIT[r]["boxcox"]["lo"] <= 0 <= FIT[r]["boxcox"]["hi"] < 1
assert not (FF["boxcox"]["lo"] <= 0 <= FF["boxcox"]["hi"] < 1)
assert RI["aggregate_out_pct"]["met"] and not RI["hcp_out_ng_mg"]["met"]
assert RI["hcp_out_ng_mg"]["p_order"] < RALPHA and RI["hcp_out_ng_mg"]["p_spread"] >= RALPHA
assert all(not RI[r]["over_f"] for r in RS)          # no run above the F median in any model
assert [(r, k) for r in RS for k in ("p_spread", "p_order") if RI[r][k] < RALPHA] == [("hcp_out_ng_mg", "p_order")]
TERMS = {r: list(FIT[r]["names"]) for r in RS}
NT = {r: len(TERMS[r]) for r in RS}
words = lambda r: join_and([tname(t) for t in TERMS[r]])
COEF = {r: FIT[r]["model"].params for r in RS}
PVAL = {r: FIT[r]["model"].pvalues for r in RS}
fold_lh = lambda r, f: float(np.exp(2 * COEF[r][f]))          # low-to-high factor of a main effect
BCX = {r: FIT[r]["boxcox"] for r in RS}
# directions the text states
bA, bH, bF, bY = (COEF[r] for r in RS)
assert bA["load"] > 0 and bA["elution_ph"] > 0 and bA["stop_collect"] > 0 and bA["stop_collect^2"] > 0
assert bA["load:elution_ph"] > 0 and bA["load:stop_collect"] > 0 and bA["elution_ph:stop_collect"] > 0
assert PVAL["aggregate_out_pct"]["wash_cond"] >= ALPHA
assert bH["load"] > 0 and bH["wash_cond"] < 0 and bH["wash_cond:elution_ph"] < 0 and bH["load^2"] < 0
assert PVAL["hcp_out_ng_mg"]["elution_ph"] >= ALPHA and PVAL["hcp_out_ng_mg"]["wash_cond:elution_ph"] < ALPHA
assert PVAL["hcp_out_ng_mg"]["load:elution_ph"] >= ALPHA and PVAL["hcp_out_ng_mg"]["load^2"] < ALPHA
assert bF["stop_collect"] > 0 and bY["load"] < 0 and "stop_collect" not in TERMS["step_yield"]
assert "elution_ph^2" not in TERMS["aggregate_out_pct"]
# residual scatter by halves of the predictions: the raw-scale full quadratic and the selected log-scale model
def _halves(m):
    fv, rv = m.fittedvalues.to_numpy(), m.resid.to_numpy()
    md = np.median(fv)
    return float(rv[fv <= md].std(ddof=1)), float(rv[fv > md].std(ddof=1))
HALF_RAW = {r: _halves(FIT[r]["full"]["model"]) for r in ("aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg")}
HALF_LOG = {r: _halves(FIT[r]["full_scale"]["model"]) for r in ("aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg")}   # full quadratic, log scale
GROW_RAW = {r: HALF_RAW[r][1] / HALF_RAW[r][0] for r in HALF_RAW}
assert all(1.0 < g < 1.10 for g in GROW_RAW.values())            # raw scatter barely grows with the level
assert all(HALF_LOG[r][1] < HALF_LOG[r][0] for r in HALF_LOG)       # log scatter smaller in the upper half
SC = D.selection_comparison().set_index("response")
SC = SC[SC["step_key"] == UO]
assert not SC.loc["aggregate_out_pct", "backward_worse"] and not SC.loc["aggregate_out_pct", "forward_worse"]
assert SC.loc["hcp_out_ng_mg", "backward_worse"] and SC.loc["hcp_out_ng_mg", "forward_worse"]
assert SC.loc["lmw_cesds_pct", "backward_worse"] and SC.loc["lmw_cesds_pct", "forward_worse"]
MA = csv("model_adequacy.csv").set_index("response")
MA = MA[MA["step_key"] == UO]
assert bool(MA.loc["aggregate_out_pct", "adequate"]) and bool(MA.loc["hcp_out_ng_mg", "adequate"])
assert not bool(MA.loc["lmw_cesds_pct", "adequate"]) and MA.loc["lmw_cesds_pct", "remedy"] == "refit"
P_AB_LOG = float(FH["full_scale"]["model"].pvalues["load:wash_cond"])
assert P_AB_LOG >= ALPHA

# --- judgements over the NOR, offsets, qualification ----------------------------------------
NORMET = {r: D.nor_met(UO, r) for r in RESPC}
assert all(NORMET.values())
UPL = {r: D.nor_prediction_limit(UO, r, "upper") for r in ("aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg")}
LOL = {r: D.nor_prediction_limit(UO, r, "lower") for r in ("aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg")}
WC = {r: D.nor_worst_corner(UO, r) for r in ("aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg")}
FRAG_MEAS = D.measured_values(UO, "lmw_cesds_pct")
assert len(FRAG_MEAS) == N_RSM and D.measured_met(UO, "lmw_cesds_pct")
OFF = {r: D.sdm_offset(UO, r) for r in ("aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg", "step_yield", "plates_per_m",
                                         "asymmetry", "dna_pool_pg_mg", "lpa_pool_ppm")}
QUAL = {r: D.offset_qualification(UO, r) for r in ("aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg")}
assert all(q["qualified"] and q["met_lo"] and q["met_point"] and q["met_hi"] for q in QUAL.values())
assert OFF["aggregate_out_pct"]["scale"] == "ratio" and OFF["hcp_out_ng_mg"]["scale"] == "ratio"
assert OFF["lpa_pool_ppm"]["scale"] == "ratio" and OFF["dna_pool_pg_mg"]["scale"] == "difference"
assert OFF["lpa_pool_ppm"]["lo"] < 1 < OFF["lpa_pool_ppm"]["hi"]
CA3S = D.ca3_criteria_sensitivity().set_index("response")
CA3S = CA3S[CA3S["step_key"] == UO]
assert not CA3S["conclusion_differs"].any() and CA3S["pars_same"].all()
assert CA3S.loc["hcp_out_ng_mg", "qualification_differs"] and not CA3S.loc["hcp_out_ng_mg", "qualified_without_ca3"]
assert abs(CA3S.loc["hcp_out_ng_mg", "criterion_without_ca3"] - float(IAC.loc["hcp_out_ng_mg", "iac_high_apriori"])) < 1e-9
# the qualification of host cell protein at the a priori criterion, with the offset at the unfavourable end
HCP_UP_SD = UPL["hcp_out_ng_mg"] * OFF["hcp_out_ng_mg"]["offset"]            # the scale-down limit
HCP_UP_LO = HCP_UP_SD / OFF["hcp_out_ng_mg"]["lo"]
assert float(IAC.loc["hcp_out_ng_mg", "iac_high_apriori"]) < HCP_UP_LO <= ACC["hcp_out_ng_mg"][1]
assert UPL["hcp_out_ng_mg"] < float(IAC.loc["hcp_out_ng_mg", "iac_high_apriori"])
# the Version 1.0 test of the qualification: a two-sample t-test of each output at p < 0.05
_q = csv("sdm_qualification.csv")
_q = _q[_q["step"] == UO]
P_V1 = {c: float(sstat.ttest_ind(_q[_q.scale == "scale-down"][c], _q[_q.scale == "manufacturing"][c]).pvalue)
        for c in ("aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg", "step_yield", "plates_per_m", "asymmetry",
                  "dna_pool_pg_mg", "lpa_pool_ppm")}
assert [c for c, p in P_V1.items() if p < ALPHA] == ["dna_pool_pg_mg"]
assert OFF["dna_pool_pg_mg"]["hi"] < 0
N_SD_Q, N_M_Q = OFF["aggregate_out_pct"]["n_sd"], OFF["aggregate_out_pct"]["n_m"]

# --- design space and proven acceptable ranges ----------------------------------------------
DSG = D.design_space_grid(UO)                 # single-batch limit (owner, 2026-10-10)
DSG_MEAN = D.design_space_grid(UO, basis="mean")
assert DSG["fraction"] == 1.0 and DSG_MEAN["fraction"] == 1.0 and all(v == 0.0 for v in DSG["per_response"].values())
assert DSG["measured"] == {"lmw_cesds_pct": True}
N_GRID = DSG["n_points"]
GRID_N = int(round(N_GRID ** (1 / len(FAC))))
PART = D.par_table(UO)
PART_M = PART[PART["Basis"] == "selected model"].reset_index(drop=True)
assert len(PART_M) == 2 * len(FAC) and (PART_M["PAR (set-point)"] == PART_M["Char. range"]).all() \
    and (PART_M["PAR (NOR)"] == PART_M["Char. range"]).all()
PAR1 = D.par_table_rev1(UO)
with D.rev1_criteria_in_force():
    PM1 = D.par_margins(UO)
PM1_OUT = PM1[~PM1["contains_nor"]].reset_index(drop=True)
_lab1 = {"aggregate_out_pct": "Aggregates (HMW, %)", "hcp_out_ng_mg": "Pool HCP (ng/mg)"}
def _par1_str(resp, f):
    row = PAR1[(PAR1["CQA"] == _lab1[resp]) & (PAR1["Parameter"] == PN[f])].iloc[0]
    s = row["PAR (NOR)"]
    return f"pH {s}" if UNIT[f] == "pH" else f"{s} {UNIT[f]}"
def _par1_v1(row):
    """A Version 1.0 range as Version 1.0 printed it, three significant digits of the unrounded ends."""
    s = f"{row['par_low']:.3g}–{row['par_high']:.3g}"
    return f"pH {s}" if UNIT[row['factor']] == "pH" else f"{s} {UNIT[row['factor']]}"

# --- doc-local model evaluation: near-equivalent models and deleted runs ------------------------
_g = list(itertools.product(*[[uo.param(f).nor[0], uo.param(f).setpoint, uo.param(f).nor[1]] for f in FAC]))
NORG = pd.DataFrame({"coded_" + f: D.to_coded(UO, f, np.array([x[i] for x in _g])) for i, f in enumerate(FAC)})
CUBEC = CUBE.rename(columns={f: "coded_" + f for f in FAC})
FEED = {"aggregate_out_pct": FEED_AGG, "hcp_out_ng_mg": FEED_HCP, "lmw_cesds_pct": FEED_FRAG}


def _off_model(resp, log):
    """The offset on the scale of a model: the mean log difference, or the difference."""
    if resp not in _q.columns:
        return 0.0
    a = _q[_q.scale == "scale-down"][resp].dropna().to_numpy(float)
    b = _q[_q.scale == "manufacturing"][resp].dropna().to_numpy(float)
    if len(a) < 2:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.log(a).mean() - np.log(b).mean()) if log else float(a.mean() - b.mean())


def evaluate(d, ycol, terms, log, resp, off_end=None):
    """One model of one output: the highest 95 % single-run limit over the NOR and over the region
    at manufacturing scale, and the clearance factor of the verification (scale-down prediction)."""
    m = sm.OLS(d[ycol].astype(float), ad.matrix(d, terms, False)).fit()
    back = np.exp if log else (lambda v: v)
    off = _off_model(resp, log)
    if off_end is not None and log:
        off = float(np.log(OFF[resp][off_end]))
    mfg = (lambda v: back(v) / np.exp(off)) if log else (lambda v: back(v) - off)
    sf = m.get_prediction(ad.matrix(NORG, terms, False)).summary_frame(alpha=1 - D.PI_LEVEL)
    sf1 = m.get_prediction(ad.matrix(NORG, terms, False)).summary_frame(alpha=2 * (1 - D.VERIFICATION_BOUND))
    sfc = m.get_prediction(ad.matrix(CUBEC, terms, False)).summary_frame(alpha=1 - D.PI_LEVEL)
    mean_sd = back(sf["mean"].to_numpy())
    i = int(np.argmax(mean_sd))
    up_c = mfg(sfc["obs_ci_upper"].to_numpy())
    # the verification converts the prediction to manufacturing scale with the offset (PCMP-001 §7.1 rule 2)
    return dict(up_nor=float(mfg(sf["obs_ci_upper"].to_numpy()).max()),
                cube_out=float((up_c > ACC[resp][1]).mean()), up_cube=float(up_c.max()),
                fold=FEED[resp] / float(mfg(sf["mean"].to_numpy())[i]),
                bound=FEED[resp] / float(mfg(sf1["obs_ci_upper"].to_numpy())[i]))


# check: the doc-local evaluation reproduces the engine for the selected models

    _e = evaluate(FIT[_r]["df"], FIT[_r]["ycol"], TERMS[_r], True, _r)
    assert abs(_e["up_nor"] - UPL[_r]) < 1e-9 * UPL[_r]
    _cq = {"aggregate_out_pct": "aggregates_hmw", "hcp_out_ng_mg": "hcp"}[_r]
    assert abs(_e["fold"] - VER.loc[_cq, "predicted_nor"]) < 1e-3 and abs(_e["bound"] - VER.loc[_cq, "predicted_nor_bound95"]) < 1e-3
_e = evaluate(FF["df"], FF["ycol"], TERMS["lmw_cesds_pct"], False, "lmw_cesds_pct")
assert abs(_e["fold"] - VER.loc["fragments_lmw", "predicted_nor"]) < 1e-3

# near-equivalent models: every hierarchical submodel within 2 AICc of the selected one, on its scale
DAICC = 2.0
NEAR = {}
for _r in ("aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg", "lmw_cesds_pct"):
    _f = FIT[_r]
    _d, _y = _f["df"], _f["df"][_f["ycol"]].to_numpy(float)
    _all = sorted(((ad.aicc(_y, ad.matrix(_d, t, False).to_numpy(float)), t) for t in ad.hierarchical_subsets(FAC)),
                  key=lambda x: x[0])
    assert abs(_all[0][0] - _f["aicc"]) < 1e-9 and _all[0][1] == TERMS[_r]
    _rows = []
    for _a, _t in [x for x in _all if x[0] <= _all[0][0] + DAICC]:
        _adq = ad.adequacy(_d, _f["ycol"], FAC, _t, D.TH)
        _log = _f["transform"] == "log"
        _e = evaluate(_d, _f["ycol"], _t, _log, _r)
        _row = dict(daicc=_a - _all[0][0], terms=_t, adequate=bool(_adq["adequate"]) and bool(_adq["f_ok"]),
                    gap=float(_adq["gap"]), p_lof=float(_adq["p_lof"]), **_e)
        if _r != "lmw_cesds_pct":
            _lo = evaluate(_d, _f["ycol"], _t, True, _r, off_end="lo")
            _hi = evaluate(_d, _f["ycol"], _t, True, _r, off_end="hi")
            _row["qualified"] = (_lo["up_nor"] <= ACC[_r][1]) == (_row["up_nor"] <= ACC[_r][1]) == (_hi["up_nor"] <= ACC[_r][1])
            _row["up_lo"] = _lo["up_nor"]
        _rows.append(_row)
    NEAR[_r] = _rows

# deleted runs: each run flagged by Cook's distance (and the run of a study event) deleted, the
# selection repeated, and the output judged over the NOR again
def delete_run(resp, run):
    d = RSM[RSM.run != run].reset_index(drop=True).copy()
    d[ad.BLOCK] = 1
    s = ad.select_model(d, resp, FAC, D.TH)
    out = dict(run=run, scale=s["scale"], terms=list(s["terms"]), adequate=bool(s["adequate"]), gap=float(s["gap"]))
    if resp in ACC:
        out.update(evaluate(s["data"], s["ycol"], list(s["terms"]), s["scale"] == "log", resp))
    return out

# screening run of DEV-007-01: its residuals, and the significant terms with and without it

S9_MFG = float(D.to_mfg(UO, "hcp_out_ng_mg", _s9["hcp_out_ng_mg"]))
R9_MFG = float(D.to_mfg(UO, "hcp_out_ng_mg", _r9["hcp_out_ng_mg"]))
_pi9 = D.prediction_interval(UO, "hcp_out_ng_mg", {f: [v] for f, v in HCP_SR_CORNER.items()})
PI9_MED, PI9_HI = float(D.to_mfg(UO, "hcp_out_ng_mg", _pi9[0])[0]), float(D.to_mfg(UO, "hcp_out_ng_mg", _pi9[2])[0])
assert S9_MFG > ACC["hcp_out_ng_mg"][1] > PI9_HI and HCP_SR_P >= ALPHA and _dl.loc[_imax] > 0
_hcp_meas_mfg = D.to_mfg(UO, "hcp_out_ng_mg", D.measured_values(UO, "hcp_out_ng_mg"))
assert int((_hcp_meas_mfg > ACC["hcp_out_ng_mg"][1]).sum()) == 1
assert all(HCP_SR_CORNER[f] in PR[f] and not (NORR[f][0] <= HCP_SR_CORNER[f] <= NORR[f][1]) for f in FAC)
_agg_meas_mfg = D.to_mfg(UO, "aggregate_out_pct", D.measured_values(UO, "aggregate_out_pct"))
assert (_agg_meas_mfg <= ACC["aggregate_out_pct"][1]).all()
S9_LOGD = float(abs(_dl.loc[_imax]))                     # the two runs at that corner, on the log scale
ELISA_LOGSD2 = float(np.sqrt(2) * np.log(1 + float(METH.loc["AMV-3012", "precision_pct"]) / 100))   # two single results
assert S9_LOGD > 3 * ELISA_LOGSD2
with D.planned_full_models():
    FULL_NOR = {r: D.nor_met(UO, r) for r in ("aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg")}
    assert D.model_status(UO, "lmw_cesds_pct") == "full"
assert all(FULL_NOR.values()) and FIT["lmw_cesds_pct"]["full"]["gap"] > GAPMAX
Q_HCP_M = _q[_q.scale == "manufacturing"]["hcp_out_ng_mg"]

# --- residual DNA and leached Protein A ------------------------------------------------------
R2 = RSM.copy()
R2[ad.BLOCK] = 1
R2["dna_cf"] = R2.dna_load_pg_mg / R2.dna_pool_pg_mg
DNA_SEL = ad.select_model(R2, "dna_cf", FAC, D.TH)
assert DNA_SEL["terms"] == [] and DNA_SEL["adequate"]
DNA_LRV = np.log10(R2["dna_cf"])
LOQ_DNA, LOQ_LPA = float(METH.loc["AMV-3014", "loq"]), float(METH.loc["AMV-3016", "loq"])
assert not RSM.dna_load_lt_loq.any() and not RSM.dna_pool_lt_loq.any() and not RSM.lpa_load_lt_loq.any()
LPA_Q = RSM[~RSM.lpa_pool_lt_loq]
LPA_C = RSM[RSM.lpa_pool_lt_loq]
N_LPA_LOQ = len(LPA_C)
LPA_CF_Q = LPA_Q.lpa_load_ppm / LPA_Q.lpa_pool_ppm
LPA_CF_C = LPA_C.lpa_load_ppm / LOQ_LPA
LPA_C_LOADS = sorted({float(v) for v in LPA_C["load"]})
N_LPA_C_HI = int((LPA_C["load"] == PR["load"][1]).sum())
LPA_FIT = D.fit(UO, "rsm", "lpa_pool_ppm")
assert LPA_FIT["names"] == ["load"] and LPA_FIT["n"] == len(LPA_Q) and LPA_FIT["model"].params["load"] > 0
LPA_PF = float(VER.loc["leached_protein_a", "assumed"])
assert min(LPA_CF_Q.min(), LPA_CF_C.min()) > LPA_PF
DNA_FIT = D.fit(UO, "rsm", "dna_pool_pg_mg")
assert DNA_FIT["names"] == []
DNA_LRV_PROC = float(CFG.raw()["process"]["cex"]["model"]["dna_lrv"])
DNA_LRV_AEX = float(CFG.raw()["process"]["aex"]["model"]["dna_lrv"])
assert DNA_LRV.min() < DNA_LRV_PROC < DNA_LRV.max()

# --- the flow-rate study (S-CEX-UNI) -------------------------------------------------------
UNI = csv("univariate_studies.csv")
UNI = UNI[UNI.step == UO].copy().reset_index(drop=True)
UNI_LV = sorted(UNI["value"].unique())
assert len(UNI_LV) == 2 and UNI_LV == list(PR["flow"]) and (UNI.groupby("value").size() == 2).all()
assert UNI["lmw_cesds_pct"].isna().all() and UNI["lmw_sec_pct"].isna().all()
UNI["dna_lrv"] = np.log10(UNI.dna_load_pg_mg / UNI.dna_pool_pg_mg)
def flow_cmp(resp):
    """High minus low end, judged with the scatter between runs of the response-surface design."""
    if resp == "dna_lrv":
        y, sd, dfr, log = UNI[resp], float(DNA_LRV.std(ddof=1)), len(R2) - 1, False
    else:
        f = FIT[resp]
        log = f["transform"] == "log"
        y, sd, dfr = (np.log(UNI[resp]) if log else UNI[resp]), float(f["rmse"]), int(f["model"].df_resid)
    lo, hi = y[UNI.value == UNI_LV[0]], y[UNI.value == UNI_LV[1]]
    diff = float(hi.mean() - lo.mean())
    se = sd * np.sqrt(1 / len(lo) + 1 / len(hi))
    hw = float(sstat.t.ppf(0.975, dfr)) * se
    p = float(2 * sstat.t.sf(abs(diff / se), dfr))
    sp = float(np.sqrt((lo.var(ddof=1) + hi.var(ddof=1)) / 2))
    p_dup = float(2 * sstat.t.sf(abs(diff / (sp * np.sqrt(1 / len(lo) + 1 / len(hi)))), len(lo) + len(hi) - 2))
    tr = (lambda v: np.exp(v)) if log else (lambda v: v)
    raw = float(UNI[resp][UNI.value == UNI_LV[1]].mean() - UNI[resp][UNI.value == UNI_LV[0]].mean())
    return dict(diff=float(tr(diff)), lo=float(tr(diff - hw)), hi=float(tr(diff + hw)), p=p, p_dup=p_dup, df=dfr, log=log, raw=raw,
                sd=sd, sd_dup=sp)
FLOW = {r: flow_cmp(r) for r in ("aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg", "step_yield", "dna_lrv")}
assert all(FLOW[r]["p"] >= ALPHA for r in ("aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg", "step_yield"))
assert FLOW["dna_lrv"]["p"] < ALPHA <= FLOW["dna_lrv"]["p_dup"] and FLOW["dna_lrv"]["diff"] < 0
assert FLOW["step_yield"]["p_dup"] < ALPHA and FLOW["step_yield"]["diff"] < 0
assert all(FLOW[r]["p_dup"] >= ALPHA for r in ("aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg"))
UNI_MFG = {r: D.to_mfg(UO, r, UNI[r].to_numpy()) for r in ("aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg")}
assert all((UNI_MFG[r] <= ACC[r][1]).all() for r in UNI_MFG)
N_UNI_LPA_LOQ = int(UNI["lpa_pool_lt_loq"].sum())
assert (UNI[UNI.value == UNI_LV[1]]["lpa_pool_lt_loq"]).all() and not (UNI[UNI.value == UNI_LV[0]]["lpa_pool_lt_loq"]).any()
SIG_MIN = {r: float(SEFF[r][SEFF[r]["p-value"] < ALPHA]["Effect"].abs().min()) for r in SRESP}
assert abs(FLOW["aggregate_out_pct"]["raw"]) < SIG_MIN["aggregate_out_pct"] and abs(FLOW["hcp_out_ng_mg"]["raw"]) < SIG_MIN["hcp_out_ng_mg"]
assert abs(FLOW["step_yield"]["raw"]) < SIG_MIN["step_yield"] < abs(FLOW["step_yield"]["lo"])
DNA_LRV_UNI_MIN = float(UNI["dna_lrv"].min())
assert DNA_LRV_UNI_MIN < DNA_LRV.min()
# the scatter of the duplicates against the residual SD of the response-surface design, per response (E5)
DUP_BIG = [r for r in FLOW if FLOW[r]["sd_dup"] > FLOW[r]["sd"]]
assert DUP_BIG == ["aggregate_out_pct", "dna_lrv"]
MARG_FLOW = NORR["flow"][0] - PR["flow"][0]
assert abs(MARG_FLOW - (PR["flow"][1] - NORR["flow"][1])) < 1e-9
# yield against the load effect: the interval of the flow comparison includes an effect as large as load's
Y_LOAD_EFF = float(SEFF["step_yield"].set_index("Term").loc["A", "Effect"])
assert FLOW["step_yield"]["lo"] < Y_LOAD_EFF < 0

# --- capability -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CAPK = ["aggregates_hmw", "hcp", "fragments_lmw", "residual_dna", "leached_protein_a"]
CAPR = cap.set_index("key")
assert (CAPR.loc[CAPK, "Cpk"] >= CPK_TARGET).all()
POOS = D.p_oos().set_index("key")
assert (POOS.loc[CAPK, "n_oos"] == 0).all()
P_UB = 1 - 0.05 ** (1 / NMC)                     # one-sided 95 % upper bound when no batch of NMC fails
CPK_LOW = min(CAPK, key=lambda k: CAPR.loc[k, "Cpk"])
MC = csv("monte_carlo.csv")
MCM = {k: float(MC[k].mean()) for k in CAPK}
MCS = {k: float(MC[k].std(ddof=1)) for k in CAPK}
assert all(abs((CQA.loc[k, "acc_high"] - MCM[k]) / (3 * MCS[k]) - CAPR.loc[k, "Cpk"]) < 0.01 * CAPR.loc[k, "Cpk"] for k in CAPK)
def msd(k):
    """Mean ± SD of the simulated batches, both to the second significant digit of the SD."""
    nd = max(0, -int(np.floor(np.log10(MCS[k]))) + 1)
    return f"{MCM[k]:.{nd}f} ± {MCS[k]:.{nd}f}"
assert CPK_LOW == "hcp"

# --- method comparability (S-CEX-FRC) ---------------------------------------------------------
FRC = csv("cex_fraction_comparability.csv")
_up = FRC["sample"].isin(["Protein A pool", "VI pool", "CEX load"])
_dn = FRC["sample"].isin(["CEX pool", "AEX pool"])
FRC_UP_MIN, FRC_UP_MAX = float(FRC[_up]["difference"].min()), float(FRC[_up]["difference"].max())
FRC_DN = float(FRC[_dn]["difference"].abs().max())
CESDS_SD = float(CFG.raw()["analytics"]["methods"]["cesds"]["sd_abs"])
SEC_SD = float(CFG.raw()["analytics"]["methods"]["sec"]["sd_abs"])
CESDS_LOQ = float(CFG.raw()["analytics"]["methods"]["cesds"]["loq"])
assert FRC_DN < FRC_UP_MIN and FRC_DN < 3 * CESDS_SD

# --- effect sizes for the text (aggregate and host cell protein at manufacturing scale) ---------
def mpred(resp, **kw):
    """The median prediction at manufacturing scale, the other factors at their set-points."""
    return D.to_mfg(UO, resp, D.predict(UO, resp, natural={**SP4, **{k: np.atleast_1d(v) for k, v in kw.items()}}))
AG_L = mpred("aggregate_out_pct", load=list(PR["load"]))
AG_P = mpred("aggregate_out_pct", elution_ph=list(PR["elution_ph"]))
AG_S = mpred("aggregate_out_pct", stop_collect=[PR["stop_collect"][0], SP["stop_collect"], PR["stop_collect"][1]])
AG_SP = float(mpred("aggregate_out_pct")[0])
HC_L = mpred("hcp_out_ng_mg", load=[PR["load"][0], SP["load"], PR["load"][1]])
HC_W = mpred("hcp_out_ng_mg", wash_cond=list(PR["wash_cond"]))
HC_SP = float(mpred("hcp_out_ng_mg")[0])
Y_SP = float(D.predict(UO, "step_yield", natural=SP4)[0])     # scale-down: yield has no criterion
Y_L = D.predict(UO, "step_yield", natural={**SP4, "load": np.array(PR["load"])})
STOP_MIN = float(D.to_natural(UO, "stop_collect", -bA["stop_collect"] / (2 * bA["stop_collect^2"])))
assert PR["stop_collect"][0] < STOP_MIN < SP["stop_collect"]
COND_F = (float(np.exp(2 * (bH["wash_cond"] - bH["wash_cond:elution_ph"]))), float(np.exp(2 * (bH["wash_cond"] + bH["wash_cond:elution_ph"]))))
LOADPH_F = (float(np.exp(2 * (bA["load"] - bA["load:elution_ph"]))), float(np.exp(2 * (bA["load"] + bA["load:elution_ph"]))))
LOADST_F = (float(np.exp(2 * (bA["load"] - bA["load:stop_collect"]))), float(np.exp(2 * (bA["load"] + bA["load:stop_collect"]))))
ELISA_RSD = float(METH.loc["AMV-3012", "precision_pct"])
HCP_WC_SD = (ACC["hcp_out_ng_mg"][1] - WC["hcp_out_ng_mg"]["predicted"]) / (ELISA_RSD / 100 * WC["hcp_out_ng_mg"]["predicted"])
AGG_WC_SD = (ACC["aggregate_out_pct"][1] - WC["aggregate_out_pct"]["predicted"]) / SEC_SD
assert HCP_WC_SD > 3 and AGG_WC_SD > 3

# --- fix pass 1 (2026-10-11): the yield stop-collect term, the host cell protein curvature, the flow-rate class ----
# yield and the stop collect: no term in the selected model, tested in the full quadratic and the screening model,
# and the selection with run 14 deleted keeps one (E9)
P_Y_STOP_FULL = float(FY["full"]["model"].pvalues["stop_collect"])
P_Y_STOP_SCR = float(SEFF["step_yield"].set_index("Term").loc["D", "p-value"])
assert P_Y_STOP_FULL >= ALPHA and P_Y_STOP_SCR >= ALPHA
_d14 = RSM[RSM.run != RUN14].reset_index(drop=True).copy()
_d14[ad.BLOCK] = 1
_s14 = ad.select_model(_d14, "step_yield", FAC, D.TH)
assert "stop_collect" in _s14["terms"] and _s14["scale"] != "log"
_m14 = sm.OLS(_s14["data"][_s14["ycol"]].astype(float), ad.matrix(_s14["data"], list(_s14["terms"]), False)).fit()
Y14_STOP, P_Y14_STOP = float(_m14.params["stop_collect"]), float(_m14.pvalues["stop_collect"])
assert Y14_STOP < 0 and P_Y14_STOP >= ALPHA
# the yield model with run 14 deleted swaps the load x conductivity interaction for a stop collect term (final pass, Q5.5:
# its stop collect values round to those of the conductivity term of the selected model by coincidence, -0.761/0.0781 against -0.757/0.0775)
Y14_TERMS = list(_s14["terms"])
Y14_DROP = [t for t in TERMS["step_yield"] if t not in Y14_TERMS]
assert Y14_DROP == ["load:wash_cond"] and [t for t in Y14_TERMS if t not in TERMS["step_yield"]] == ["stop_collect"]
assert DEL14["step_yield"]["terms"] == Y14_TERMS
# the host cell protein curvature in load against the spread of the centre points (PCP-007 §12) (E10)
HCP_CURV = float(bH["load^2"])
HCP_CP_LNSD = float(np.log(RSM[RSM.run_type == "center"]["hcp_out_ng_mg"]).std(ddof=1))
assert abs(HCP_CURV) < HCP_CP_LNSD
N_NEAR_NOCURV = sum("load^2" not in x["terms"] for x in NEAR_ALT["hcp_out_ng_mg"])
assert N_NEAR_NOCURV >= 1
# the least favourable host cell protein combination names only the factors in the model (E13)
HCP_FAC = [f for f in FAC if any(f in t.replace("^2", "").split(":") for t in TERMS["hcp_out_ng_mg"])]
assert HCP_FAC == ["load", "wash_cond", "elution_ph"]
# elution flow rate and residual DNA: the size of the effect against the drug substance (C, owner 2026-10-11)
DNA_FLOW_F = float(10 ** (-FLOW["dna_lrv"]["diff"]))                    # lower clearance at the high end, as a factor
DNA_FLOW_F_NOR = float(10 ** (-FLOW["dna_lrv"]["diff"] * (NORR["flow"][1] - NORR["flow"][0]) / (PR["flow"][1] - PR["flow"][0])))
DNA_DS_AT_F = MCM["residual_dna"] * DNA_FLOW_F
CPK_DNA_AT_F = (float(CQA.loc["residual_dna", "acc_high"]) - DNA_DS_AT_F) / (3 * MCS["residual_dna"] * DNA_FLOW_F)   # level and SD scaled alike
assert DNA_DS_AT_F < float(CQA.loc["residual_dna", "acc_high"]) and CPK_DNA_AT_F > CPK_TARGET

LAB = {"aggregate_out_pct": T.ATTR_NAME["aggregates_hmw"], "hcp_out_ng_mg": T.ATTR_NAME["hcp"],
       "lmw_cesds_pct": T.ATTR_NAME["fragments_lmw"], "step_yield": "Step yield (%)"}
```

# Executive summary {.unnumbered}

Cation exchange chromatography is Step 7 of the A-Mab drug substance process and its principal aggregate polishing step. The antibody is bound to the resin and eluted by a step change in pH, and the step clears host cell protein, residual DNA, leached Protein A and part of the fragments. It sets no quality attribute of its own. This report presents the Stage 1 characterization of the step under the plan PCP-007 [@fda2011]. The characterization studies ran from `{python} CHAR_START` to `{python} CHAR_END` on a scale-down model of the commercial column, for a process that runs at a production bioreactor scale of `{python} f"{SCALE_L:,}"` L at the commercial site in `{python} RECEIVING_LOCATION`. During the re-analysis, two studies of the low-pH viral inactivation report ran this step on the same scale-down model, at its set-point and on material from the low-pH step, to test how well it clears aggregate and fragments. They are S-CEX-VER, from `{python} win('S-CEX-VER')`, and S-VI-WC, from `{python} win('S-VI-WC')`.

Protein load, load/wash conductivity, elution buffer pH and elution stop collect were studied in a two-level full factorial screening design of `{python} N_SCR` runs and in a face-centred central composite design of `{python} N_RSM` runs. Elution flow rate was assessed one factor at a time. The scale-down model is qualified for aggregate and host cell protein by its offsets from manufacturing scale, and every judgement of those two outputs is stated at manufacturing scale. Each output is judged against an intermediate acceptance criterion. The a priori criterion is the value derived before the studies, from the drug substance criterion and the platform worst cases of the later steps. The criterion in force is that value after this campaign's data on the later steps tightened or widened it. For host cell protein the qualification holds at the criterion in force of `{python} C_HCP` ng/mg and would not hold at the a priori criterion of `{python} C_HCP_AP` ng/mg.

Aggregate and host cell protein met their intermediate acceptance criteria at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high. The single-run limit is the upper end of the `{python} PI_PCT` % prediction interval of a single run, at manufacturing scale. Its highest value over the NOR was `{python} num(UPL['aggregate_out_pct'])` % for aggregate against `{python} C_AGG` %, and `{python} num(UPL['hcp_out_ng_mg'])` ng/mg for host cell protein against `{python} C_HCP` ng/mg. The aggregate criterion is the drug substance criterion of `{python} C_AGG_AP` % less the largest rise expected across UF/DF, `{python} f"{UFDF_ADD:.3f}"` percentage points. Fragments have no adequate model and were judged on their measured results, which lay between `{python} num(FRAG_MEAS.min())` % and `{python} num(FRAG_MEAS.max())` % against `{python} C_FRAG` %. On the single-run limit and at the criteria in force, the design space covers the whole characterized region. At the a priori host cell protein criterion it would cover `{python} f"{100 * DS_AP:.2f}"` % of it. The proven acceptable range of every parameter for aggregate and host cell protein is its range studied.

The models of aggregate and host cell protein were selected on the log scale and meet the first three adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2. The host cell protein model does not meet the fourth, because its residuals drift with the order of execution. That drift amounts to a factor of `{python} f"{HCP_DRIFT_F:.2f}"` over the study. The highest single-run limit over the NOR stays below the criterion with the whole drift added to it. The highest limit over the whole region studied would not, and nor would the limit over the NOR with the offset at the unfavourable end of its interval, on which the qualification rests (@sec-rsm-hcp). Of the `{python} N_PAR` parameters, `{python} N_WC` were classified as well-controlled critical process parameters. Elution flow rate was classified as a general process parameter, by a judgement of the practical relevance of its effect on residual DNA (@sec-classification).

Within its NOR the step cleared aggregate less than the platform worst case on which the criteria upstream rely. At manufacturing scale the lowest clearance factor predicted was `{python} num(VER.loc['aggregates_hmw', 'predicted_nor'])` against `{python} num(VER.loc['aggregates_hmw', 'assumed'])`. The one-sided `{python} VB_PCT` % prediction bound of a single batch, `{python} num(VER.loc['aggregates_hmw', 'predicted_nor_bound95'])`, replaced the platform value and tightened the aggregate criteria of the low-pH pool and the bioreactor harvest. The platform worst case for host cell protein was confirmed with the offset at its estimate. It would not be confirmed with the offset at the unfavourable end of its interval, or under `{python} len(HCP_ALT_NC)` of the `{python} len(NEAR_ALT['hcp_out_ng_mg'])` other models within `{python} f"{DAICC:g}"` AICc units of the selected model. The platform worst case for fragments was confirmed by the rule of PCP-007 §7.6, which confirms a platform worst case when the lowest clearance factor predicted within the NOR is not below it. The fragment model behind that prediction does not meet PCMP-001 §7.2. Leached Protein A is not a response of the designs.

The capability indices of the drug substance attributes that the step clears all exceed the target of `{python} CPK_TARGET`, and the lowest is `{python} f"{CAPR.loc[CPK_LOW, 'Cpk']:.2f}"` for host cell protein. No simulated batch of `{python} f"{NMC:,}"` fell outside its criterion. The capability of the step itself, which the plan asked for, was not estimated.

Version 1.0 recorded `{python} N_DEV` events of execution, which this report keeps as study events under their Version 1.0 DEV numbers. Screening run `{python} RUN6` used a load/wash buffer from an expired lot (DEV-007-01), and the column inlet temperature rose above its set-point during response-surface run `{python} RUN14` (DEV-007-02). Both runs were retained in the analysis. The register records `{python} N_PD` discrepancies from the plan. Four concern the analysis and the scale-down model. They are the model selection, conclusions that rest on a model that does not meet the criterion on residuals, the flow-rate study without its set-point run, and the residual DNA offset, which was recorded and not investigated. Five concern records the plan required that are not in the study record. These are the load results for aggregate and host cell protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A on the screening runs, the flow-through, wash and strip fractions with the mass balance, the packing tests of each campaign, and the feed lots. The other two are the fractionated runs of S-CEX-FRC, which no version of the plan foresaw, and the approaches this report takes where the plan sets no threshold, with capability given for the drug substance and not for the step. The last corrects an error of Version 1.0 of this report, which named the acetate load/wash buffer of screening run `{python} RUN6` a Tris buffer.

# Introduction {#sec-intro}

## Product and unit operation {#sec-product}

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody developed on the Novacyte platform [@amab2009]. Its drug substance is purified by Protein A chromatography, low-pH viral inactivation, cation exchange chromatography, anion exchange chromatography, small-virus retentive filtration and ultrafiltration/diafiltration. Cation exchange is Step 7 of this train. It receives the neutralized pool of the low-pH viral inactivation step and passes its eluate pool to anion exchange.

The step is operated in bind and elute mode on a resin with a sulfonate ligand. Below its isoelectric point the antibody carries a net positive charge and binds the ligand. After a wash at the conductivity of the load, the antibody is eluted by a step change to the elution buffer, whose pH weakens the binding. The pool is collected between a threshold on the ascending edge of the elution peak and the stop collect threshold on the descending edge, both read as absorbance at 280 nm. Aggregate binds more strongly than monomer and elutes later, so the step separates the two by where the pool is cut. Host cell protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A that do not bind, or bind only weakly, leave in the load flow-through and the wash.

No quality attribute is set at this step. Aggregate is formed in the production bioreactor and added to during the low-pH hold. No later step removes aggregate, and UF/DF adds a little within its NOR. The pool of this step is therefore judged against the drug substance criterion less the largest rise expected across UF/DF (@sec-basis). Host cell protein is cleared here and again at anion exchange. No viral clearance is claimed for cation exchange. Enveloped virus is claimed at low-pH inactivation, anion exchange and virus filtration, and small viruses at anion exchange and virus filtration [@ichq5a].

The process is being transferred from the development site in `{python} SENDING_LOCATION` to the commercial drug substance site in `{python} RECEIVING_LOCATION` under the Process Transfer Plan PTP-001. It operates there at a production bioreactor scale of `{python} f"{SCALE_L:,}"` L. @tbl-related lists the documents this report depends on and the document it rolls up into.

```{python}

print(related_docs_md(DOC))
print()
print(": Documents related to this report. {#tbl-related}")
```

## Objectives {#sec-objectives}

PCP-007 §2 sets six objectives. Objectives 2 and 3 were amended at Version 2.0 of the plan to include fragments, and objective 6 was added.

1. "To quantify the relationship between each studied parameter and each response of the step, over ranges wider than the ranges in which the step will be operated."
2. "To define the multivariate region over which the fitted models predict that the aggregate, the host cell protein and the fragment content of the eluate pool all meet the criteria in Table 7.1" of the plan.
3. "To establish a proven acceptable range for each parameter against the aggregate, the host cell protein and the fragment content of the pool, both with the rest of the step at target and with the rest of the step varying within its normal operating ranges."
4. "To classify each parameter under SOP-4001, from the size of its demonstrated effect and from the capability with which the parameter is controlled."
5. "To state the ranges, in-process controls and monitoring this step contributes to the control strategy, and to justify them for Stage 2."
6. "To verify the platform worst cases of cation exchange on which the criteria upstream rely."

@sec-conclusions states the outcome against each objective.

## Regulatory and scientific basis {#sec-basis-reg}

The study belongs to Stage 1 of process validation, in which the commercial process is defined from development knowledge and the studies that support it are recorded [@fda2011]. It follows the enhanced approach of ICH Q8(R2) [@ichq8] and ICH Q11 [@ichq11]. Prior knowledge and the risk assessment RA-001 identified the parameters that may affect the quality attributes, and the designed experiments measured and bounded those effects. Criticality is treated as a continuum, as described in ICH Q8(R2), within the risk management principles of ICH Q9(R1) [@ichq9]. The process model, the attribute framework and the risk methodology come from the A-Mab case study [@amab2009]. The designs and their analysis follow standard response surface practice [@montgomery2017].

The master plan PCMP-001 sets the common approach of the campaign, and PCP-007 applies it to this step. Where this report states a rule, it cites the section of the plan or the master plan that sets it. The controlled procedures and method validations that governed the work are listed in @tbl-sops. The SOP and AMV numbers are placeholders.

Version 1.0 of this report was approved on `{python} REV1['effective']`. Version 2.0, effective `{python} doc_version(DOC)[1]`, is issued under two Quality Assurance (QA) investigations. `{python} INV['id']` (`{python} INV['title']`) was opened on `{python} INV['opened']` after a review of PCMR-001 Version 1.0 for the Biologics License Application (BLA). It was closed on `{python} INV['closed']` with the classification `{python} INV['classification']`. It found that the criteria used to judge each step in the proven acceptable range analysis had been set after the data were seen and appeared in no approved plan (INV-001 finding 1). `{python} INV2['id']` (`{python} INV2['title']`) judged the response-surface models of the outputs with a criterion against the first three model adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2. Its corrective action CA3, adopted on `{python} CA3_DATE`, analyses every response-surface output by model selection.

This revision changes the report in seven ways.

1. The acceptance criteria. Version 1.0 judged the pool against an aggregate limit of `{python} R1_AGG` % and a host cell protein limit of `{python} R1_HCP` ng/mg. Version 2.0 judges the pool against the intermediate acceptance criteria of PCMP-001 §7.3, derived from the drug substance criteria and the platform worst cases of the later steps (@sec-basis). @tbl-criteria-change compares the two versions. Two criteria in force differ from their a priori values. The host cell protein criterion is wider than its a priori value of `{python} C_HCP_AP` ng/mg, and @sec-basis argues that change by its risk. The aggregate criterion is tighter than the drug substance criterion of `{python} C_AGG_AP` % by the rise that UF/DF may add (@sec-basis).
2. Fragments. Fragments are judged at this step for the first time, against the drug substance criterion, on results by non-reduced capillary electrophoresis with sodium dodecyl sulfate (nrCE-SDS) under the analytical method decision `{python} AMD['id']` (@sec-analytical).
3. The models. Every output of the response-surface design is analysed by model selection instead of the full quadratic model of the plan (discrepancy PD-007-01, @sec-statistics).
4. The scale-down model. The model is qualified for each output by its offset from manufacturing scale, not by a test of equivalence, and every judgement of an output with a measured offset is made at manufacturing scale (@sec-sdm).
5. The judgement. Each quality attribute is judged on the `{python} PI_PCT` % prediction interval of a single run, and the design space is drawn on the same statistic (@sec-statistics).
6. The verification. The report verifies the platform worst cases of cation exchange on which the criteria upstream rely (@sec-verification).

The events of execution that Version 1.0 recorded are reported as study events under their Version 1.0 numbers, and the departures from the plan as discrepancies (@sec-record). # Prior knowledge and quality risk basis {#sec-prior}

## Platform and prior-product knowledge {#sec-platform}

The cation exchange step has been operated on the Novacyte humanized IgG1 platform for three earlier products, X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab, and throughout A-Mab clinical and engineering manufacture [@amab2009]. The resin chemistry, the buffer system and the mode of operation are unchanged for A-Mab. This experience establishes the mechanisms of the step and identified the parameters worth studying. It also supplies the platform worst cases from which the criteria are derived (@sec-basis and @sec-verification).

Aggregate presents more positive charge to the ligand than monomer does, so it is retained more strongly and elutes on the tail of the elution peak. The clearance of aggregate depends on how well the two species are resolved and on where collection stops. At the load pH, host cell proteins with an isoelectric point below that pH carry a net negative charge and leave in the load flow-through. Those with an isoelectric point above it bind with the antibody. The weakly bound among them are displaced in the wash, and the rest are separated from the antibody in the elution. A part of the host cell protein is held in association with the bound antibody and elutes with it. DNA carries a strong negative charge and is repelled by the ligand, so its clearance is large and is not expected to depend on the parameters studied. Free leached Protein A does not bind under load conditions, but the leached Protein A in complex with the antibody binds with it, which limits the clearance to a modest factor. Fragments carry less positive charge than intact antibody and elute on the leading side of the main peak. Yield is lost at both edges of the pool, before collection starts and after it stops.

PCP-007 §4.1 draws four expectations from this experience, and the multivariate designs were built to test them.

1. A higher protein load occupies more of the ligand. The monomer and aggregate peaks broaden and overlap, and more host cell protein is held with the bound antibody, so aggregate and host cell protein in the pool are expected to rise and yield to fall as load rises.
2. A higher load/wash conductivity is expected to strip more of the weakly bound host cell protein in the wash and to have little effect on the aggregate separation. The ionic strength of the load and the wash does not change the relative charge of aggregate and monomer at the elution pH, and that difference in charge is what separates them.
3. A higher elution buffer pH weakens binding and brings monomer and aggregate off closer together, so it is expected to raise aggregate in the pool.
4. The stop collect point is an absorbance on the descending edge, so a lower setting stops collection later. Stopping later is expected to take in more monomer and the leading part of the aggregate peak, which raises both the yield and the aggregate of the pool, and to add eluate that carries few fragments.

The plan adds that a higher conductivity is expected to remove more host cell protein at a high load than at a low one, and that elution flow rate, within its range, is expected to change the sharpness of the peak too little to move the aggregate content of the pool. Curvature was expected in the effects of elution stop collect and elution buffer pH (PCP-007 §6.3). The stop collect moves the end of the pool along the falling edge of the peak. The elution buffer pH changes the charge of the antibody, and so the position and the width of the peak against the collection thresholds. Because the aggregate peak has a maximum, equal steps in either setting add unequal amounts of aggregate to the pool.

## Quality attributes in scope {#sec-cqas}

The drug substance register assigns no quality attribute to this step. Aggregate is formed in the production bioreactor, host cell protein and residual DNA enter with the harvested cell culture fluid, leached Protein A is released at capture, and fragments form in culture and during the harvest hold. @tbl-cqas lists the five attributes the step clears, with their drug substance criteria and their criticality. Criticality was assigned with Tool #1 of the case study, which combines the impact of an attribute with the uncertainty in that impact [@amab2009].

```{python}
#| output: asis
_c = cqas_by_keys(["aggregates_hmw", "fragments_lmw", "hcp", "residual_dna", "leached_protein_a"]).copy()
_c["Category"] = _c["Category"].str.capitalize()
_c = _c[["Category", "CQA", "Acceptance", "Criticality", "Tool #1"]]
T.frame(_c, "Quality attributes in scope at cation exchange, with their drug substance criteria and criticality.",
        "tbl-cqas", merge=["Category"], header={"Acceptance": "Drug substance\ncriterion", "Tool #1": "Tool #1\nscore"},
        align=["l", "P{4.6cm}", "l", "c", "r"],
        notes=[("", "VL, very low. L, low. M, moderate. H, high. A paired code such as M-H means moderate to high.")],
        notes_per_row=True).show()
```

Three of the five attributes are responses of the designs. Aggregate has the highest criticality of the five and is the attribute the step exists to control. Host cell protein is cleared here and at anion exchange, so the pool of this step must be one that anion exchange can bring to the drug substance criterion. Fragments were measured by nrCE-SDS in the response-surface design (@sec-analytical). Residual DNA and leached Protein A were measured across the step so that their clearance is known. The plan does not treat them as responses of the designs, and it claims a parameter dependence for neither unless the data show one. The residual DNA criterion of ≤ `{python} f"{float(CQA.loc['residual_dna', 'acc_high']):g}"` ng per dose is the acceptable range that the case study claims for A-Mab in its Table 2.17. It is set far below the 10 ng per dose recommended by the World Health Organization, which the case study cites [@amab2009]. Step yield is a process performance attribute. It has no acceptance criterion, and it is read together with aggregate because the monomer cut away with the aggregate is lost from the pool.

## Risk-based prioritization and parameter selection {#sec-risk}

All process parameters of the step were carried into the risk ranking and filtering of RA-001 [@ichq9]. Each parameter was ranked for its potential impact on a quality attribute and for its potential to interact with other parameters, and a parameter with no data or rationale was ranked at the highest level [@amab2009]. The assignment produced three groups.

1. Protein load, load/wash conductivity, elution buffer pH and elution stop collect were assigned to the multivariate designs. The first, third and fourth move the aggregate peak against the stop point, and load acts with conductivity on the host cell protein that survives the wash, so their effects cannot be assumed to add.
2. Elution flow rate was assigned to a univariate assessment. It acts on the separation through the residence time of the antibody in the column and the rate of mass transfer into and out of the resin, and within its range these were expected to change the sharpness of the elution peak only a little.
3. Parameters fixed by equipment design or held to platform specification, such as bed height, packing quality and buffer composition, were assigned no new study. Their ranges rest on the platform knowledge and on the procedures in @tbl-sops.

The range studied of each parameter is wider than its NOR at both ends (@tbl-params). The ranges were set from the control capability of the commercial equipment and from the range over which the platform has been operated, so that the study bounds the step beyond the region in which it runs [@ichq8]. The elution buffer pH range stops short of incomplete elution at its low end and of the co-elution of aggregate with monomer at its high end.

# Materials and methods {#sec-methods}

## Scale-down model and its qualification {#sec-sdm}

The scale-down model is a laboratory column of the commercial resin type, packed to the commercial bed height and run at the commercial linear velocities (SOP-1001, SOP-2010). Load is expressed in grams of antibody per litre of resin and every buffer volume in column volumes, so each parameter of the study has its commercial value.

The qualification study S-CEX-SDM ran from `{python} win('S-CEX-SDM')`, before the first characterization run on `{python} CHR.loc['S-CEX-SCR', 'start']`. It compared `{python} N_SD_Q` scale-down runs at the set-point with `{python} N_M_Q` A-Mab batches at manufacturing scale. The outputs compared were step yield, pool aggregate, pool host cell protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A, together with plate count and peak asymmetry (PCP-007 §5.1).

The offset of an output is the mean of the scale-down runs minus the mean of the manufacturing batches, with its two-sided `{python} CI_PCT` % confidence interval (PCMP-001 §7.1). For an output modelled on the log scale the offset is taken on that scale. It is then the ratio of the scale-down to the manufacturing geometric mean, and a scale-down value is divided by it to give the manufacturing-scale value. The model is qualified for an output with a criterion when the conclusion over the NOR is the same with the offset at either end of its interval. An output with no criterion at this step has its offset recorded only. @tbl-sdm-offsets gives the offsets.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.sdm_offsets(["cex"]).show()
```

The model is qualified for both outputs that carry a criterion. The aggregate ratio is `{python} f"{OFF['aggregate_out_pct']['offset']:.3f}"` (`{python} CI_PCT` % CI `{python} f"{OFF['aggregate_out_pct']['lo']:.3f}"` to `{python} f"{OFF['aggregate_out_pct']['hi']:.3f}"`). The host cell protein ratio is `{python} f"{OFF['hcp_out_ng_mg']['offset']:.3f}"` (`{python} f"{OFF['hcp_out_ng_mg']['lo']:.3f}"` to `{python} f"{OFF['hcp_out_ng_mg']['hi']:.3f}"`). That interval is wide, because it rests on `{python} N_SD_Q` and `{python} N_M_Q` runs and the manufacturing batches ranged from `{python} num(Q_HCP_M.min())` to `{python} num(Q_HCP_M.max())` ng/mg. The qualification for host cell protein depends on the criterion it is judged against. With the offset at the unfavourable end of its interval, the highest single-run limit over the NOR is `{python} num(HCP_UP_LO)` ng/mg. That meets the criterion in force of `{python} C_HCP` ng/mg and would not meet the a priori criterion of `{python} C_HCP_AP` ng/mg. Under the a priori criterion the model would therefore not be qualified for host cell protein, and @sec-basis argues the change of criterion on which the qualification rests. @sec-near gives the sensitivity of this qualification to the choice among the models within `{python} f"{DAICC:g}"` AICc units of the selected one.

Among the outputs without a criterion, only residual DNA differed between the scales at the level of the two-sample t-test of Version 1.0 (`{python} pq(P_V1['dna_pool_pg_mg'])`, against `{python} pq(min(v for k, v in P_V1.items() if k != 'dna_pool_pg_mg'))` at the lowest for the other outputs compared). The scale-down pools carried `{python} f"{-OFF['dna_pool_pg_mg']['offset']:.1f}"` pg/mg less residual DNA than the manufacturing pools (`{python} CI_PCT` % CI `{python} f"{-OFF['dna_pool_pg_mg']['hi']:.1f}"` to `{python} f"{-OFF['dna_pool_pg_mg']['lo']:.1f}"` pg/mg less). Version 1.0 of the plan required the cause of such a difference to be established before characterization went on, and it was not (discrepancy PD-007-04, @sec-record). Residual DNA has no criterion at this step, so no conclusion of this report depends on its offset.

The qualification did not compare fragments at both scales, so their offset is unknown, not zero. Fragments are judged as the scale-down model gives them (PCMP-001 §7.1). That rests on the assumption, stated in PCP-007 §12, that fragments separate in the same way at both scales. The scale-down column keeps the bed height, the linear velocity and the collection thresholds of the commercial column, and its plate count and peak asymmetry did not differ from manufacturing scale at the level of the Version 1.0 test (@tbl-sdm-offsets).

The centre-point runs of both designs were made at the set-point of every factor. Their spread measures the reproducibility of the model under study conditions and gives the pure error against which lack of fit is tested (@sec-centre). The scale-down column reproduces the chromatography of the commercial column, but not the hold times, pool volumes or mixing of the commercial suite. The conclusions of this report apply to the commercial step through the qualification above, and they are to be confirmed at scale in Stage 2.

## Operation {#sec-operation}

Each run followed the operation of SOP-2010. The neutralized low-pH pool was brought to the load conductivity of the run and applied to the equilibrated column up to the protein load of the run. The wash used the same conductivity, because the platform holds load and wash conductivity equal, and the two were therefore varied as one factor. The antibody was eluted by a step change to the elution buffer of the run, and the pool was collected from a threshold on the rising edge of the peak to the stop collect threshold on its falling edge, both read as OD280. Strip, sanitization and re-equilibration followed SOP-2008. Buffer composition, packing and resin storage were not varied.

PCP-007 §5.1 required plate count and asymmetry to be tested, and the column released against SOP-2008, before each campaign. Plate count and asymmetry are recorded for the `{python} N_SD_Q` scale-down runs of the qualification only, with no acceptance limits. No packing result is recorded for the screening, response-surface and flow-rate campaigns (discrepancy PD-007-08). PCP-007 §6.2 also required the feed lot of every run to be recorded. The record does not name the feed lot of any run (discrepancy PD-007-11).

@tbl-windows gives the execution window of each study made on the scale-down model of this step. The record names an instrumented system for the response-surface study only, the `{python} EQ['description']` `{python} EQ.name`. It was in calibration for the whole study, which closed on `{python} CHR.loc['S-CEX-RSM', 'end']`, before its next calibration fell due on `{python} EQ['cal_due']`. Every characterization study of the step closed by `{python} CHAR_END`, before Version 1.0 of this report was approved.

The screening design ran before the method decision `{python} AMD['id']` of `{python} AMD['date']`, and the response-surface design ran across it (@sec-analytical). Two studies of the low-pH viral inactivation report made cation exchange runs on this scale-down model after INV-001 closed.
