## Analytical methods {#sec-analytical}

Every response was measured by a validated method, listed in @tbl-sops and Appendix D. Pool aggregate was measured by size exclusion chromatography (SEC, AMV-3011) and reported as the percentage of high molecular weight species. Host cell protein was measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA, AMV-3012) and reported per milligram of antibody, so that the value does not move with the concentration of the pool. Residual DNA was measured by quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR, AMV-3014) and leached Protein A by ELISA (AMV-3016). Step yield was calculated from the antibody mass in the load and in the pool, each from its absorbance at 280 nm. Appendix D gives the performance of each method.

Fragments are judged on nrCE-SDS results only (AMV-3020, under SOP-3015). From `{python} AMD['date']` every study that measures fragments, at every step, measures them by nrCE-SDS, so that one method spans the train (`{python} AMD['id']`, PCMP-001 §7.8). @tbl-methods-by-study shows which method measured fragments in which design of this step. The screening design ran before the decision and has SEC fragment results only. Its samples were not retained for a retest by nrCE-SDS, and its SEC fragment results are kept in the record and are not used for any decision. The response-surface design measured fragments by both methods on every run. The flow-rate study measured no fragments, because Version 1.0 of the plan listed none for it.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.methods_by_study(["cex"]).show()
```

The decision followed the comparability study S-CEX-FRC (`{python} win('S-CEX-FRC')`), in which SEC and nrCE-SDS were run on the same samples (@tbl-sec-cesds). The samples included the fractions F2 to F5 of a run of this step with the eluate collected in fractions, which were collected to read the elution profile against the stop collect. No version of the plan foresaw this study (discrepancy PD-007-09). SEC read fragments high wherever the sample still carried host cell protein, because the part of the host cell protein that elutes in the low molecular weight window of SEC is counted as fragment. In the Protein A pool, the viral inactivation pool and the cation exchange load it was `{python} f"{FRC_UP_MIN:.2f}"` to `{python} f"{FRC_UP_MAX:.2f}"` percentage points. From the cation exchange pool onward the two methods agreed to within `{python} f"{FRC_DN:.2f}"` points (INV-001 finding 6). SEC remains the method for aggregate, where no such interference applies.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.method_comparability().show()
```

Assay variability is part of the residual variance of each model and of the centre-point spread. A response measured by a less precise assay therefore carries a wider prediction interval and a less sensitive test of lack of fit. The ELISA for host cell protein has a precision of `{python} f"{ELISA_RSD:g}"` % relative standard deviation (RSD), and the centre points show host cell protein as the least reproducible response (@sec-centre).

## Sampling plan {#sec-sampling}

PCP-007 §5.4 sampled each run at four points. The load after conditioning was to give the aggregate, host cell protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A entering the step. The flow-through and the wash were each to be sampled as one pooled fraction, to close the host cell protein mass balance. The eluate pool was to carry every response, and a strip fraction was to be retained and tested only where a run failed to close its mass balance.

The record of the designs holds the pool results of every run. It holds residual DNA and leached Protein A in the load and the pool of every response-surface run and of every run of the flow-rate study, and in the pools of the qualification runs. Three parts of the sampling plan are not in the record.

1. No load result for aggregate or host cell protein is recorded for any run (discrepancy PD-007-05). The clearance factors for aggregate and host cell protein in this report are therefore calculated against the level that the nominal batch of the process model brings to the step, as the verification rule of PCP-007 §7.6 specifies, and not against a measured load.
2. Residual DNA and leached Protein A were not measured on the screening runs (discrepancy PD-007-06).
3. No result for the flow-through, wash or strip fractions is recorded, so no mass balance was made and the strip test could not be triggered (discrepancy PD-007-07).

Version 1.0 of this report stated that the load, the flow-through and the wash were assayed, with no result recorded.

Replication is concentrated at the centre point. The screening design carries `{python} NC_SCR` centre-point runs and the response-surface design carries `{python} NC_RSM`. The record holds the order of execution of every run. The centre points ran at positions `{python} join_and(CO_SCR)` of `{python} N_SCR` in the screening design and at positions `{python} join_and(CO_RSM)` of `{python} N_RSM` in the response-surface design.

## Statistical methods {#sec-statistics}

All factors were analysed in coded units. Each factor is coded so that its set-point is 0 and the ends of its range studied are −1 and +1. At this step the set-point of every factor is the centre of its range, so the design centre and the set-point coincide. The letter codes of @tbl-legend are used for the model terms.

The screening design was analysed by ordinary least squares with all main effects and all two-factor interactions. An effect is twice the coded coefficient, the change in the response across the whole range of the factor, and a term is significant at p < `{python} f"{ALPHA:g}"` (PCMP-001 §6.2). The screening model identifies effects. It is not the predictive model of the step, because a model without quadratic terms cannot describe curvature.

The response-surface model is the predictive model. Every judgement over the NOR, every proven acceptable range, the design space and the verification of the platform worst cases come from it. The plan prescribed the full quadratic model of each output, with `{python} N_FULL` terms besides the intercept (PCP-007 §5.5). Each output was instead analysed by the model selection of INV-002 corrective action CA3, in three steps (discrepancy PD-007-01).

1. The scale was chosen from the Box-Cox profile of the full quadratic [@boxcox1964]. The log scale is used where the `{python} PI_PCT` % interval of the Box-Cox exponent λ contains 0 and excludes 1, and the raw scale otherwise.
2. On that scale, every hierarchical submodel of the full quadratic was fitted, `{python} f"{N_CAND:,}"` candidates for four factors, and the one with the lowest corrected Akaike information criterion (AICc) was taken. A hierarchical model keeps the main effects of any interaction or square it contains.
3. The selected model was judged against the four adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2. An output whose selected model fails one of the first three criteria has no adequate model. It is judged on its measured results and sets no range.

AICc is the small-sample form of Akaike's criterion [@hurvich1989], and selecting a model by such a criterion is standard practice [@burnham2002]. It estimates how well a model would predict new runs. It rewards a close fit and penalizes every estimated term, and the residual variance is counted as one of those terms. Its correction for small samples raises the penalty when the runs are few for the number of terms, as they are in a design of `{python} N_RSM` runs, so that the criterion does not favour too many terms. The search is exhaustive because a stepwise search changes one term at a time and stops when no single change lowers AICc, which can leave it short of a model that only a combination of changes reaches. On the data of this step a stepwise search, backward or forward, would have reached the selected model for aggregate. For host cell protein a backward search would have stopped at a model of `{python} int(SC.loc['hcp_out_ng_mg', 'backward_terms'])` terms and a forward search at one of `{python} int(SC.loc['hcp_out_ng_mg', 'forward_terms'])`, with AICc values of `{python} fm(SC.loc['hcp_out_ng_mg', 'backward_aicc'], 1)` and `{python} fm(SC.loc['hcp_out_ng_mg', 'forward_aicc'], 1)` against `{python} fm(SC.loc['hcp_out_ng_mg', 'aicc'], 1)` for the selected model, and for fragments both would have stopped at a model with a higher AICc. In this report the terms of a model are counted without the intercept.

The Box-Cox profile chose the log scale for aggregate (λ = `{python} fm(BCX['aggregate_out_pct']['lambda'])`, `{python} PI_PCT` % interval `{python} fm(BCX['aggregate_out_pct']['lo'])` to `{python} fm(BCX['aggregate_out_pct']['hi'])`) and for host cell protein (λ = `{python} fm(BCX['hcp_out_ng_mg']['lambda'])`, interval `{python} fm(BCX['hcp_out_ng_mg']['lo'])` to `{python} fm(BCX['hcp_out_ng_mg']['hi'])`). It kept the raw scale for fragments, whose interval contains 1. On the log scale the model is $\ln y = b_0 + b_1 x_1 + \dots + \varepsilon$. Transformed back, $y = e^{b_0} \, e^{b_1 x_1} \cdots e^{\varepsilon}$, so each parameter multiplies the output by a fixed factor $e^{b}$ per coded unit, and by $e^{2b}$ from the low to the high end of its range. The scatter between runs multiplies the output too, so its size in the unit of the output grows with the level. This is the behaviour expected of a purification step, which removes a share of what is present, so that a parameter changes the share rather than a fixed amount. It is also expected of a method whose precision is a percentage of the level, as the ELISA for host cell protein is.

Least squares, and the t-tests, F-tests and prediction intervals built on it, assume residuals that are independent and normally distributed, with mean zero and the same variance over the whole range studied. For these two outputs the evidence for the log scale is the Box-Cox profile. The residuals themselves do not show the scatter growing with the level on the raw scale. For the full quadratic on the raw scale, the residual SD in the upper half of the predictions is only `{python} f"{100 * (GROW_RAW['aggregate_out_pct'] - 1):.0f}"` % larger than in the lower half for aggregate and `{python} f"{100 * (GROW_RAW['hcp_out_ng_mg'] - 1):.0f}"` % larger for host cell protein. For the full quadratic on the log scale it is smaller in the upper half (`{python} f"{HALF_LOG['aggregate_out_pct'][1]:.3f}"` against `{python} f"{HALF_LOG['aggregate_out_pct'][0]:.3f}"` for aggregate). At `{python} N_RSM` runs neither difference is large enough to decide the scale. The regression of the absolute residuals on the predicted values, one of the tests of the fourth criterion, finds no trend in the selected log-scale model of either output (@tbl-resid).

On the log scale the criteria stay in their own units, % and ng/mg. Effects are fold changes, and @sec-rsm gives them. A prediction interval is calculated on the log scale and transformed back, which keeps its `{python} PI_PCT` % coverage, because the probability that ln y lies between two values is the probability that y lies between their antilogs. The interval is asymmetric. At the least favourable NOR combination for host cell protein the median is `{python} num(WC['hcp_out_ng_mg']['predicted'])` ng/mg and the interval runs from `{python} num(WC['hcp_out_ng_mg']['pi_low'])` to `{python} num(WC['hcp_out_ng_mg']['pi_high'])` ng/mg, further above the median than below it. The predicted value is the median of the output, its geometric mean, not its arithmetic mean. The upper prediction limit, which decides against an upper criterion, is not affected by that.

Each model is reported with R², adjusted R² and predicted R², the last from the prediction error sum of squares. The four adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2 are applied as PCP-007 §7.2 states them as tests.

1. The model F-test is significant at α = `{python} f"{ALPHA:g}"`.
2. Lack of fit against the pure error of the centre points is not significant at α = `{python} f"{LOFA:g}"`.
3. Predicted R² falls short of R² by no more than `{python} f"{GAPMAX:.2f}"`. This is the limit on overfitting. A model that fits its own runs much better than it predicts runs left out of the fit has more terms than the data support.
4. The absolute residuals regressed on the predicted values, and the residuals regressed on the order of execution, show no slope significant at α = `{python} f"{RALPHA:g}"`. A run with a Cook's distance above `{python} f"{COOKF:g}"`/n is examined by deleting it and repeating the judgement, and the model fails this criterion only where a run's Cook's distance exceeds the median of the F distribution with p and n − p degrees of freedom.

A model with no term has no F-test, so the first criterion does not apply to it. An output with a selected model that fails the fourth criterion is still used for the ranges and the design space, and that use is discrepancy PD-007-02. For each such model this report states the size of the trend against the criterion of its output, and it deletes each flagged run in turn, repeats the selection and judges the output over the NOR again. Where other models lie within `{python} f"{DAICC:g}"` AICc units of the selected one, they are reported as a sensitivity, and the selected model decides.

A quality attribute is judged on a single batch. The judgement over the NOR asks whether the exact `{python} PI_PCT` % prediction interval of a single run, at manufacturing scale, lies within the criterion at every one of the `{python} len(NORG)` combinations of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the four factors (PCP-007 §7.4). The interval is two-sided, so its upper end is a one-sided `{python} f"{PI_UP:g}"` % limit, and since every criterion at this step is an upper limit, the upper end decides. The design space is the set of settings within the ranges studied at which every output with a criterion meets it at both ends of the same interval. It is evaluated on a grid of `{python} GRID_N` levels per factor, `{python} f"{N_GRID:,}"` points in all.

Two proven acceptable ranges are computed for each parameter and each output with a criterion and an adequate model (PCMP-001 §6.4). The set-point analysis scans the parameter across its range with the other factors at their set-points and judges the mean prediction, which is the median for a log-scale model, at manufacturing scale. The NOR-propagated analysis scans the parameter at `{python} PAR_GRID` points and draws, at each, `{python} f"{PAR_N:,}"` settings of the other factors, each from a normal distribution centred on its set-point, with a standard deviation equal to the width of its NOR divided by `{python} f"{NOR_DIV:g}"`, and clipped to the range studied. Each draw takes its own fitted coefficients from their sampling distribution and its own residual. A setting is accepted where the `{python} f"{PI_UP:g}"`th percentile of the simulated batches, at manufacturing scale, does not exceed the criterion. The range reported is the contiguous accepted interval that contains the set-point. The simulation uses the fixed seed `{python} MC_SEED`. The NOR-propagated range is the one that supports a claim.

The verification of the platform worst cases follows PCP-007 §7.6. The clearance factor is the level that the nominal batch of the process model brings to the step divided by the pool level that the response-surface model predicts. For aggregate and host cell protein the prediction is first converted to manufacturing scale with the offset at its estimate, as PCMP-001 §7.1 rule 2 requires of every judgement against a criterion. Fragments have no measured offset and enter as the scale-down model gives them. The model gives the lowest clearance factor over the `{python} len(NORG)` combinations of the NOR and the one-sided `{python} VB_PCT` % prediction bound of a single batch at the least favourable combination. Capability is estimated for the drug substance from the integrated model of the train, which simulates `{python} f"{NMC:,}"` batches with every parameter drawn within its NOR (PCMP-001 §6.5), and is judged against the target capability index of `{python} CPK_TARGET` and the minimum of `{python} CPK_MIN` (PCMP-001 §7.9). PCP-007 §5.5 also asked for the capability of the step, from the fitted models over draws within the NOR. It was not estimated (discrepancy PD-007-10).

### Decisions for which the plan sets no threshold {#sec-thresholds}

PCP-007 §7 lists six decisions of Version 1.0 for which no numerical threshold was set, and PCP-007 §8 leaves a seventh to this report. The approach this report takes for each is as follows. Three of the decisions could not be made as planned, because the records they need are missing. The approaches and those three gaps are recorded as discrepancy PD-007-10.

1. A parameter dependence of residual DNA or leached Protein A "unless the data show one" (PCP-007 §4.2). In the response-surface design the clearance factor of residual DNA was analysed by the same model selection as every output, and a dependence would be shown by a selected model with a term that meets PCMP-001 §7.2. Leached Protein A could not be analysed in that way, because `{python} N_LPA_LOQ` of its `{python} N_RSM` pool results lie below the limit of quantitation (LOQ) and a model of the others leaves them out. In the flow-rate study a dependence is judged by the difference between the results at the two ends of the range, with its 95 % confidence interval, as in item 5.
2. The repacking of a column that fails the packing tests (PCP-007 §5.1). The record holds plate count and peak asymmetry for the qualification runs only, with no limits, so no repacking decision can be reviewed (PD-007-08).
3. The attribution to the assay of a predicted value within assay variability of its criterion (PCP-007 §5.3). The distance of a prediction from its criterion is expressed in standard deviations (SD) of the precision of its method at that level.
4. The test of the strip fraction where a run fails to close its mass balance (PCP-007 §5.4). The record holds no flow-through, wash or strip result, so no mass balance was made and the test could not be triggered (PD-007-07).
5. The move of elution flow rate into a multivariate study after an effect "comparable in size with the effects estimated in the screening study" (PCP-007 §6.4). For each response of the flow-rate study, the difference between the mean results at the two ends of its range is given with its 95 % confidence interval (CI). The CI uses the residual SD of the same response in the response-surface design, with that design's degrees of freedom, and the difference is set against the smallest effect found significant for the response in the screening design.
6. The identification of runs made on a lot "out of trend" (PCP-007 §12). The record names no feed lot for any run of the designs (PD-007-11), and the load results that would show a lot out of trend are not recorded either (PD-007-05). This decision could therefore not be made.
7. The judgement of the flow-rate range against the criteria (PCP-007 §8). The range is supported for an attribute when every individual result at both ends, at manufacturing scale, meets its criterion. It is not supported for an attribute the study did not measure.

# Study design {#sec-design}

## Factors, ranges and the knowledge space {#sec-factors}

@tbl-params gives the five parameters with their set-points, NORs, ranges studied, classes and study types. The range studied is the knowledge space of the step. The NOR is the range in which routine manufacture is controlled, and the classes are the outcome of @sec-classification.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_p = RP.rename(columns={"Char. range": "Range studied", "Study": "Study type"}).copy()
_p["Set-point"] = [f"{v:g}" for v in _p["Set-point"]]
_p["Study type"] = _p["Study type"].str.capitalize()
T.frame(_p, "Parameters of the cation exchange step, with the NOR, the range studied and the class.", "tbl-params",
        align=["P{3.6cm}", "P{2.6cm}", "r", "l", "l", "l", "l"]).show()
```

The four multivariate parameters enter both designs as the coded factors of @tbl-legend.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_lg = D.factor_legend_df(UO)[["Code", "Factor", "Unit"]]
T.frame(_lg, "Coded factors of the screening and response-surface designs.", "tbl-legend", align=["c", "l", "l"]).show()
```

## Screening design {#sec-screening-design}

The screening study S-CEX-SCR ran from `{python} win('S-CEX-SCR')`. It is a two-level full factorial in the four factors, `{python} NF_SCR` runs, with `{python} NC_SCR` centre-point runs, `{python} N_SCR` runs in all. A full factorial was chosen over a fraction because protein load was expected to interact with each of the other three factors. It estimates every main effect and every two-factor interaction independently. The runs were executed in a randomized order, with the centre points at the positions given in @sec-sampling. Appendix A gives the design and its results.

## Response-surface design {#sec-rsm-design}

The response-surface study S-CEX-RSM ran from `{python} win('S-CEX-RSM')`. It is a face-centred central composite design in the same four factors, with `{python} NF_RSM` factorial runs, `{python} NA_RSM` axial runs and `{python} NC_RSM` centre-point runs, `{python} N_RSM` runs in all. The axial runs sit on the faces of the cube, so no run lies outside the range studied of any factor. The design adds the quadratic terms that the screening design cannot estimate. All four screening factors were carried into it. The design therefore did not need the augmentation that PCP-007 §6.3 requires when an active screening factor is left out of the response-surface design. Appendix B gives the design and its results.

## Univariate assessment {#sec-univariate}

The flow-rate study S-CEX-UNI ran from `{python} win('S-CEX-UNI')`, within the window of the response-surface study. Elution flow rate was run at each end of its range, `{python} pset('flow', UNI_LV[0])` and `{python} pset('flow', UNI_LV[1])`, in duplicate, with every other parameter at its set-point. The plan also required a run at the set-point, which was not made, and the qualification runs at the set-point serve as the reference instead (discrepancy PD-007-03). Pool aggregate, pool host cell protein, step yield, and residual DNA and leached Protein A in the load and the pool were measured on each run. A study of one factor at a time cannot show whether flow rate interacts with the other parameters. That limit was accepted because flow rate sets the residence time in the resin, and with it the sharpness of the peak, while it changes neither the charge of the antibody nor the ionic strength that holds it to the ligand.

# Results {#sec-results}

## Centre-point performance and reproducibility {#sec-centre}

@tbl-centre gives the mean, SD and coefficient of variation of the centre points of both designs. These runs measure the reproducibility of the scale-down model under study conditions, and their spread is the pure error of the test for lack of fit.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_rows = []
for _kind, _name in (("screening", "Screening"), ("rsm", "Response surface")):
    _cv = D.center_cv_df(UO, _kind)
    for _r, (_, _x) in zip(["aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg", "step_yield"], _cv.iterrows()):
        _k = 100.0 if _r == "step_yield" else 1.0
        _rows.append([_name, LAB[_r], str(int(_x["n"])), num(_x["Mean"] * _k), num(_x["SD"] * _k), f"{_x['%CV']:.1f}"])
_cvd = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=["Design", "Response", "Runs", "Mean", "SD", "CV (%)"])
CVS = {(_d, _r): float(_c) for _d, _r, _c in zip(_cvd["Design"], _cvd["Response"], _cvd["CV (%)"])}
T.frame(_cvd, "Centre-point reproducibility of the two designs.", "tbl-centre", merge=["Design"],
        align=["P{2.6cm}", "P{4.6cm}", "r", "r", "r", "r"],
        notes=[("", "CV, coefficient of variation (SD divided by the mean).")], notes_per_row=True).show()
```

Host cell protein was the least reproducible response in both designs, with a coefficient of variation of `{python} f"{CVS[('Screening', LAB['hcp_out_ng_mg'])]:.1f}"` % in the screening design and `{python} f"{CVS[('Response surface', LAB['hcp_out_ng_mg'])]:.1f}"` % in the response-surface design. This agrees with the expectation of PCP-007 §5.3. Aggregate varied by `{python} f"{CVS[('Screening', LAB['aggregate_out_pct'])]:.1f}"` % and `{python} f"{CVS[('Response surface', LAB['aggregate_out_pct'])]:.1f}"` %, and step yield by `{python} f"{CVS[('Screening', LAB['step_yield'])]:.1f}"` % and `{python} f"{CVS[('Response surface', LAB['step_yield'])]:.1f}"` %. The pure error has `{python} FS['aggregate_out_pct']['df_pe']` degrees of freedom in the screening design and `{python} FA['df_pe']` in the response-surface design, so the tests for lack of fit are of modest power.

@tbl-scr-fit summarises the screening models. Each model is significant, and none shows significant lack of fit. With `{python} FS['aggregate_out_pct']['df_pe']` degrees of freedom for pure error that test is weak, and the models are read for the effects they identify, not for prediction.

```{python}
_e = {r: SEFF[r].set_index("Term") for r in SRESP}
ea = lambda t: num(_e["aggregate_out_pct"].loc[t, "Effect"])
```

Aggregate was impacted by protein load, elution buffer pH and elution stop collect. Across the range studied, load raised pool aggregate by `{python} ea('A')` percentage points (`{python} pa('A')`), pH by `{python} ea('C')` points (`{python} pa('C')`) and stop collect by `{python} ea('D')` points (`{python} pa('D')`). Significant interactions were found between load and pH (`{python} ea('AC')` points), load and stop collect (`{python} ea('AD')` points) and pH and stop collect (`{python} ea('CD')` points). Load/wash conductivity had no significant effect on aggregate (`{python} pa('B')`).

Host cell protein was impacted by load/wash conductivity and protein load. Across the range, conductivity lowered pool host cell protein by `{python} num(-_e['hcp_out_ng_mg'].loc['B', 'Effect'])` ng/mg (`{python} ph_('B')`) and load raised it by `{python} eh('A')` ng/mg (`{python} ph_('A')`), with a significant negative interaction between them (`{python} eh('AB')` ng/mg, `{python} ph_('AB')`). On the raw scale, two effects that are additive on the log scale appear as an interaction, and with one effect positive and the other negative that interaction is negative. The response-surface analysis on the log scale examines whether a load × conductivity term remains (@sec-rsm). Step yield fell with protein load by `{python} num(-100 * _e['step_yield'].loc['A', 'Effect'])` percentage points across the range (`{python} pq(_e['step_yield'].loc['A', 'p-value'])`), and no other term was significant. Appendix C gives every effect.

The `{python} NF_SCR` factorial runs of the screening design repeat the corners of the response-surface design. Over those corners the host cell protein results of the two designs did not differ systematically, with a geometric mean ratio of `{python} f"{HCP_SR_RATIO:.2f}"` (screening to response surface, `{python} pq(HCP_SR_P)`). The largest difference was at the corner of `{python} corner(HCP_SR_CORNER)`. There, screening run `{python} S9_RUN` gave `{python} num(S9_MFG)` ng/mg at manufacturing scale and response-surface run `{python} R9_RUN` gave `{python} num(R9_MFG)` ng/mg, a factor of `{python} f"{HCP_SR_MAXF:.1f}"`. The screening result is the one result of either design above its criterion of `{python} C_HCP` ng/mg. It lies above the upper `{python} PI_PCT` % single-run limit that the response-surface model gives at that corner, `{python} num(PI9_HI)` ng/mg. The corner lies outside the NOR of all four parameters. On the log scale the two runs differ by `{python} f"{S9_LOGD:.2f}"`, against `{python} f"{ELISA_LOGSD2:.2f}"` for one standard deviation of the difference between two single ELISA results, so the precision of the method does not explain the difference. The record gives no cause for it, and this report offers none. The response-surface model stays the predictive model, and @sec-ds states what the result means for the design space.

## Response-surface models {#sec-rsm}

@tbl-model-summary gives the selected model of each output of the response-surface design against the adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2. The models of aggregate and host cell protein meet the first three criteria. The aggregate model also meets the fourth, and the host cell protein model does not. The selected fragment model fails the limit on overfitting, so fragments have no adequate model. Step yield has no criterion and is reported for information.

```{python}

for _r in RS:

                  f"{_f['p_lof']:.3f}", "met" if _ri["met"] else "not met", _st])
_ms = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=["Output", "Scale", "Terms", "R²", "Adj.\nR²", "Pred.\nR²", "Gap", "Model\np",
                                   "Lack of\nfit p", "Crite-\nrion 4", "Ade-\nquate"])
T.frame(_ms, "Selected response-surface models against the adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2.", "tbl-model-summary",
        align=["P{3.0cm}", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "l", "l"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", f"Terms, without the intercept. Adj., adjusted. Pred., predicted. Gap, R² minus predicted R², at most {GAPMAX:.2f}. Criterion 4, the residuals and influential runs. Adequate, the first three criteria met. Step yield has no criterion.")],
```

The plan's full quadratic model was adequate on the planned runs for aggregate and host cell protein, and the selection removed terms the data do not support (@tbl-reeval-cex). For fragments the full quadratic failed the limit on overfitting by a wide margin. INV-002 assigned that model a refit, because no augmentation within the size of the planned design reached the required probability of success. Under corrective action CA3 the fragment model was selected instead, and the selected model of `{python} NT['lmw_cesds_pct']` terms also fails the limit. This step was not augmented.

```{python}
T.model_reevaluation("cex").show()
```

### Aggregate {#sec-rsm-agg}

The aggregate model on the log scale has `{python} NT['aggregate_out_pct']` terms, `{python} words('aggregate_out_pct')`. It explains `{python} f"{100 * FA['R2']:.1f}"` % of the variation (adjusted R² `{python} f"{FA['adjR2']:.3f}"`, predicted R² `{python} f"{FA['predR2']:.3f}"`). The model F-test is significant (`{python} pq(FA['p'])`), lack of fit is not (`{python} pq(FA['p_lof'])`), and predicted R² falls short of R² by `{python} f"{FA['gap']:.3f}"`. The residuals show no trend against the predicted values (`{python} pq(RI['aggregate_out_pct']['p_spread'])`) or the order of execution (`{python} pq(RI['aggregate_out_pct']['p_order'])`). Runs `{python} join_and(RI['aggregate_out_pct']['over'])` have a Cook's distance above `{python} f"{COOKF:g}"`/n = `{python} f"{RI['aggregate_out_pct']['cook_limit']:.3f}"`, the largest `{python} f"{RI['aggregate_out_pct']['cook_max']:.2f}"` for run `{python} RI['aggregate_out_pct']['cook_run']`, and none exceeds the median of F(p, n − p), `{python} f"{RI['aggregate_out_pct']['f_limit']:.2f}"`.

From the low to the high end of its range, protein load multiplies pool aggregate by `{python} f"{fold_lh('aggregate_out_pct', 'load'):.2f}"`, elution buffer pH by `{python} f"{fold_lh('aggregate_out_pct', 'elution_ph'):.2f}"` and elution stop collect by `{python} f"{fold_lh('aggregate_out_pct', 'stop_collect'):.2f}"`, each with the other factors at their set-points. There the interactions do not act, and a curvature term has the same value at both ends of a range, so these factors are the full change across the range. The conductivity term, kept by the selection, has `{python} pq(PVAL['aggregate_out_pct']['wash_cond'])` and a factor of `{python} f"{fold_lh('aggregate_out_pct', 'wash_cond'):.2f}"`, so no effect of conductivity on aggregate is demonstrated. The interactions make load act more strongly at a high pH and at a high setting of the stop collect. From the low to the high end of the load range, aggregate rises by a factor of `{python} f"{LOADPH_F[0]:.2f}"` at `{python} pset('elution_ph', PR['elution_ph'][0])` and by `{python} f"{LOADPH_F[1]:.2f}"` at `{python} pset('elution_ph', PR['elution_ph'][1])`. The stop collect has a significant curvature, and with the other factors at their set-points aggregate is lowest near `{python} f"{STOP_MIN:.2f}"` AU. No curvature in pH was found. @tbl-rsm-coef gives the coefficients and @tbl-anova the analysis of variance.

```{python}

        _rows.append([LAB[_r], _x["Term"], f"{_x['Coef.']:.4f}".replace("-", "−"), f"{_x['Std. err.']:.4f}",
                      f"{_x['t']:.2f}".replace("-", "−"), pq(_x['p-value']).replace('p = ', '').replace('p ', '')])
_cd = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=["Output", "Term", "Coefficient", "SE", "t", "p"])
T.frame(_cd, "Coefficients of the selected models of aggregate and host cell protein (log scale, coded units).",
        "tbl-rsm-coef", merge=["Output"], align=["P{3.6cm}", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r"],

        notes_per_row=True).show()
```

### Host cell protein {#sec-rsm-hcp}

The host cell protein model on the log scale has `{python} NT['hcp_out_ng_mg']` terms, `{python} words('hcp_out_ng_mg')`. It explains `{python} f"{100 * FH['R2']:.1f}"` % of the variation (adjusted R² `{python} f"{FH['adjR2']:.3f}"`, predicted R² `{python} f"{FH['predR2']:.3f}"`). The model F-test is significant (`{python} pq(FH['p'])`), lack of fit is not (`{python} pq(FH['p_lof'])`), and predicted R² falls short of R² by `{python} f"{FH['gap']:.3f}"`. The model does not meet the fourth criterion. Its residuals fall with the order of execution (`{python} pq(RIH['p_order'])`), although they show no trend against the predicted values (`{python} pq(RIH['p_spread'])`). Runs `{python} join_and(RIH['over'])` have a Cook's distance above `{python} f"{RIH['cook_limit']:.3f}"`, the largest `{python} f"{RIH['cook_max']:.2f}"` for run `{python} RIH['cook_run']`, and neither exceeds the median of F(p, n − p), `{python} f"{RIH['f_limit']:.2f}"`.

From the low to the high end of its range, with the other factors at their set-points, protein load multiplies pool host cell protein by `{python} f"{fold_lh('hcp_out_ng_mg', 'load'):.2f}"` and load/wash conductivity multiplies it by `{python} f"{fold_lh('hcp_out_ng_mg', 'wash_cond'):.2f}"`. The two effects are of the same size within their standard errors. With the other factors at their set-points the model gives `{python} num(HC_L[0])`, `{python} num(HC_L[1])` and `{python} num(HC_L[2])` ng/mg at manufacturing scale for loads of `{python} pset('load', PR['load'][0])`, `{python} pset('load', SP['load'])` and `{python} pset('load', PR['load'][1])`, and `{python} num(HC_W[0])` and `{python} num(HC_W[1])` ng/mg at conductivities of `{python} pset('wash_cond', PR['wash_cond'][0])` and `{python} pset('wash_cond', PR['wash_cond'][1])`. The selected model keeps a negative curvature in load (`{python} pq(PVAL['hcp_out_ng_mg']['load^2'])`). Its coefficient, `{python} fm(HCP_CURV, 3)` on the log scale, is smaller than the SD of the centre points on the same scale, `{python} f"{HCP_CP_LNSD:.3f}"`, and `{python} N_NEAR_NOCURV` of the `{python} len(NEAR_ALT['hcp_out_ng_mg'])` other models within `{python} f"{DAICC:g}"` AICc units leave it out (@sec-near). PCP-007 §12 states that an effect smaller than the spread of the centre points will not be claimed, so the curvature is kept in the model for prediction and is not claimed as a finding. Elution buffer pH has no significant main effect (`{python} pq(PVAL['hcp_out_ng_mg']['elution_ph'])`), but it changes the effect of conductivity (`{python} pq(PVAL['hcp_out_ng_mg']['wash_cond:elution_ph'])`). From the low to the high end of the conductivity range, host cell protein falls by a factor of `{python} f"{COND_F[0]:.2f}"` at `{python} pset('elution_ph', PR['elution_ph'][0])` and of `{python} f"{COND_F[1]:.2f}"` at `{python} pset('elution_ph', PR['elution_ph'][1])`. The load × pH term is kept with `{python} pq(PVAL['hcp_out_ng_mg']['load:elution_ph'])`. On the log scale the full quadratic gives the load × conductivity term `{python} pq(P_AB_LOG)`, so the interaction the screening design found on the raw scale is not found on the log scale.

@fig-diag-hcp shows the diagnostics of the host cell protein model.

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Diagnostics of the selected host cell protein model (log scale), with the residuals against the predicted values, a normal probability plot and the measured against the predicted values."
_ = D.fig_diagnostics(UO, "hcp_out_ng_mg")
plt.show()
```

@fig-hcp-order plots the residuals of the host cell protein model against the order of execution. The slope is `{python} fm(RIH['order_slope'], 4)` per run on the log scale, so that over the `{python} f"{RIH['order_range']:.0f}"` positions of the study the residuals fell by `{python} f"{abs(HCP_DRIFT):.3f}"`, a factor of `{python} f"{HCP_DRIFT_F:.2f}"` between the first and the last run at the same settings. The record gives no cause for the drift. Added in full to the highest single-run limit over the NOR, `{python} num(UPL['hcp_out_ng_mg'])` ng/mg, it gives `{python} num(HCP_UPL_DRIFT)` ng/mg against `{python} C_HCP` ng/mg. The conclusion over the NOR therefore does not depend on the trend. Outside the NOR it can. Added to the highest single-run limit over the whole region studied, `{python} num(CUBE_UP['hcp_out_ng_mg'][0])` ng/mg, the drift gives `{python} num(HCP_DS_DRIFT)` ng/mg, and `{python} f"{100 * DS_DRIFT_OUT:.2f}"` % of the grid would then exceed the criterion. Added to the highest limit over the NOR with the offset at the unfavourable end of its interval, `{python} num(HCP_UP_LO)` ng/mg, it gives `{python} num(HCP_UP_LO_DRIFT)` ng/mg, so with the drift the qualification for host cell protein would not hold. The edge of the design space and the qualification for host cell protein are therefore sensitive to the drift, whose cause is unknown.

### Influential runs {#sec-influence}

Each run with a Cook's distance above `{python} f"{COOKF:g}"`/n was deleted in turn, the model selection was repeated on the other `{python} N_RSM - 1` runs, and the output was judged over the NOR again (@tbl-deletion). With any one of these runs deleted, aggregate and host cell protein still meet their criteria over the NOR, the whole region studied still meets them on the single-run limit, and the verification of their platform worst cases gives the same outcome as in @sec-verification. The terms of the selected models do change. Every deletion changes the aggregate model, and deleting run `{python} DEL_RAW['aggregate_out_pct'][0]` moves it to the raw scale. Deleting run `{python} RIH['over'][0]` or run `{python} RIH['over'][1]` moves the host cell protein model to the raw scale, where it keeps a load × conductivity interaction, as the screening analysis on the raw scale did. The choice of scale for host cell protein therefore rests on these two runs, and no conclusion over the NOR rests on that choice.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_rows = []
for _r in ("aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg"):
    for _x in DEL[_r]:
        _rows.append([LAB[_r], str(_x["run"]), _x["scale"], str(len(_x["terms"])), num(_x["up_nor"]),
                      f"{100 * (1 - _x['cube_out']):.0f}", num(_x["fold"]), num(_x["bound"])])
    _f = FIT[_r]
    _e0 = evaluate(_f["df"], _f["ycol"], TERMS[_r], True, _r)
    _rows.insert(len(_rows) - len(DEL[_r]), [LAB[_r], "none", "log", str(NT[_r]), num(_e0["up_nor"]),
                                             f"{100 * (1 - _e0['cube_out']):.0f}", num(_e0["fold"]), num(_e0["bound"])])
_dd = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=["Output", "Run\ndeleted", "Scale", "Terms", "Highest single-run\nlimit over the NOR",
                                   "Region inside\n(%)", "Lowest clearance\nfactor in the NOR", "Bound of a\nsingle batch"])
T.frame(_dd, "Selection repeated with each flagged run deleted.", "tbl-deletion", merge=["Output"],
        align=["P{3.0cm}", "c", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", "Limits at manufacturing scale, in the unit of the output. Region inside, the share of the grid over the region studied at which the single-run limit meets the criterion. Clearance factor and bound as in the verification of the platform worst cases (one-sided bound of a single batch), at manufacturing scale.")],
        notes_per_row=True).show()
```

### Models within two AICc units of the selected model {#sec-near}

Other models lie within `{python} f"{DAICC:g}"` AICc units of the selected one for both outputs (@tbl-near). For aggregate, the one other model differs only by leaving out the conductivity main effect, and it gives the same conclusions. For host cell protein, `{python} len(NEAR_ALT['hcp_out_ng_mg'])` other models differ in the load × pH term and in curvature in load and pH. All of them meet the first three adequacy criteria and give the same judgement over the NOR.

Three results differ among the host cell protein models. First, `{python} len(HCP_ALT_OUT)` of the `{python} len(NEAR_ALT['hcp_out_ng_mg'])` other models put a small part of the region studied outside the criterion on the single-run limit, at most `{python} f"{100 * max(x['cube_out'] for x in HCP_ALT_OUT):.2f}"` % of the grid. That part lies at the lowest conductivity and at loads of `{python} pset('load', HCP_ALT_LOADMIN)` and above. Second, `{python} len(HCP_ALT_UNQ)` models give a highest single-run limit over the NOR above the criterion of `{python} C_HCP` ng/mg with the offset at the unfavourable end of its interval, up to `{python} num(max(x['up_lo'] for x in HCP_ALT_UNQ))` ng/mg. Under them the scale-down model would not be qualified for host cell protein. Third, `{python} len(HCP_ALT_NC)` models give a lowest clearance factor within the NOR of `{python} num(min(x['fold'] for x in HCP_ALT_NC))` to `{python} num(max(x['fold'] for x in HCP_ALT_NC))`, below the platform worst case of `{python} num(VER.loc['hcp', 'assumed'])`. Under any of them, rule 1 of PCMP-001 §7.5 would replace the platform value with the bound of a single batch and tighten the host cell protein criterion of the Protein A pool. They show that the qualification for host cell protein, the verification of its platform worst case and the edge of the design space at that corner all lie close to their limits.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_rows = []
for _r in ("aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg"):

    for _x in NEAR[_r]:
        _t = set(_x["terms"])
        _diff = " ".join([("+" + D._term_label(t, LET)) for t in sorted(_t - _sel)] + [("−" + D._term_label(t, LET)) for t in sorted(_sel - _t)])
        _rows.append([LAB[_r], f"{_x['daicc']:.2f}", _diff or "selected model",
                      f"{_x['gap']:.3f}", num(_x["up_nor"]), "Yes" if _x["qualified"] else "No",
                      f"{100 * _x['cube_out']:.2f}", num(_x["fold"])])
_nd = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=["Output", "AICc\nabove best", "Terms added (+)\nor removed (−)", "Gap",
                                   "Limit over\nthe NOR", "Qualified", "Region\noutside (%)",
                                   "Clearance\nfactor"])
T.frame(_nd, "Models within two AICc units of the selected model.", "tbl-near", merge=["Output"],
        align=["P{2.4cm}", "r", "P{3.0cm}", "r", "r", "c", "r", "r"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", "Letters as in the coefficient table. Gap, R² minus predicted R². Limit over the NOR, the highest single-run limit at manufacturing scale. Qualified, the conclusion over the NOR the same with the offset at either end of its interval. Region outside, the share of the grid over the region studied at which the single-run limit exceeds the criterion. Clearance factor, the lowest within the NOR, as in the verification of the platform worst cases at manufacturing scale. Every model shown meets the first three adequacy criteria.")],
        notes_per_row=True).show()
```

### Fragments {#sec-rsm-frag}

Fragments have no adequate model. The selected model keeps `{python} words('lmw_cesds_pct')` on the raw scale. Its F-test is significant (`{python} pq(FF['p'])`) and lack of fit is not (`{python} pq(FF['p_lof'])`), but predicted R² falls short of R² by `{python} f"{FF['gap']:.3f}"`, above the limit of `{python} f"{GAPMAX:.2f}"`. The only other model within `{python} f"{DAICC:g}"` AICc units fails the same limit. Fragments are therefore judged on their measured results, and no range and no predicted level is derived for them. Every one of the `{python} len(FRAG_MEAS)` nrCE-SDS results of the response-surface design lay between `{python} num(FRAG_MEAS.min())` % and `{python} num(FRAG_MEAS.max())` %, below the criterion of `{python} C_FRAG` %, at settings that span the range studied of all four parameters.

The gap of the fragment model lies close to its limit. With run `{python} FRAG_DEL_ADQ[0]` or run `{python} FRAG_DEL_ADQ[-1]` deleted the same terms would meet it. The stop collect term of the fragment model has the direction expected in @sec-platform, fragments rising as the stop collect setting rises and collection stops earlier, but no effect on fragments is claimed from a model that does not meet PCMP-001 §7.2.

### Step yield {#sec-rsm-yield}

Step yield has no criterion. Its selected model on the raw scale keeps `{python} words('step_yield')` and explains `{python} f"{100 * FY['R2']:.1f}"` % of the variation. With the other factors at their set-points the model gives `{python} num(100 * Y_SP)` % in the scale-down model, and from `{python} num(100 * Y_L[0])` % to `{python} num(100 * Y_L[1])` % across the load range. The selected model has no stop collect term. The stop collect was also tested directly. Its term has `{python} pq(P_Y_STOP_FULL)` in the plan's full quadratic and its effect `{python} pq(P_Y_STOP_SCR)` in the screening model, so no effect of the stop collect on yield was detected. The selection is sensitive to one run. Run `{python} RUN14` is the run with the temperature excursion. With it deleted, the selection keeps `{python} join_and([tname(t) for t in Y14_TERMS])` and drops the `{python} tname(Y14_DROP[0])` interaction. In that model the stop collect term is `{python} fm(100 * Y14_STOP)` percentage points per coded unit (`{python} pq(P_Y14_STOP)`), yield falling as the setting rises, which is the direction the mechanism expects (@sec-dev02).

## Residual DNA and leached Protein A {#sec-dna-lpa}

Residual DNA was quantified in the load and the pool of all `{python} N_RSM` response-surface runs. The load carried `{python} num(RSM.dna_load_pg_mg.min())` to `{python} num(RSM.dna_load_pg_mg.max())` pg/mg and the pool `{python} num(RSM.dna_pool_pg_mg.min())` to `{python} num(RSM.dna_pool_pg_mg.max())` pg/mg, so the step cleared `{python} f"{DNA_LRV.min():.2f}"` to `{python} f"{DNA_LRV.max():.2f}"` log10 (mean `{python} f"{DNA_LRV.mean():.2f}"`). The selected model of the clearance factor, on the log scale, has no term. Within the range studied, therefore, the clearance of residual DNA does not depend on any of the four parameters, at the precision of these runs and of the qPCR method (`{python} f"{float(METH.loc['AMV-3014', 'precision_pct']):g}"` % RSD). The process model credits the step with `{python} f"{DNA_LRV_PROC:g}"` log10, within the range measured. Appendix B gives the result of every run.

Leached Protein A was quantified in the load of every run, at `{python} num(RSM.lpa_load_ppm.min())` to `{python} num(RSM.lpa_load_ppm.max())` ppm. In `{python} N_RSM - N_LPA_LOQ` pools it was quantified at `{python} num(LPA_Q.lpa_pool_ppm.min())` to `{python} num(LPA_Q.lpa_pool_ppm.max())` ppm, a clearance factor of `{python} num(LPA_CF_Q.min())` to `{python} num(LPA_CF_Q.max())`. In the other `{python} N_LPA_LOQ` pools it lay below the LOQ of `{python} num(LOQ_LPA)` ppm, so their clearance factors are known only to exceed `{python} num(LPA_CF_C.min())` to `{python} num(LPA_CF_C.max())`. The model selection applied to the `{python} N_RSM - N_LPA_LOQ` quantified pools chooses the log scale and keeps protein load (`{python} pq(float(LPA_FIT['model'].pvalues['load']))`), pool leached Protein A rising with load. That fit leaves out the `{python} N_LPA_LOQ` results below the LOQ, which were at loads of `{python} join_and([pset('load', v) for v in LPA_C_LOADS])` and include `{python} N_LPA_C_HI` at the highest load, so the data do not show a dependence on load, and none is claimed. The offset of leached Protein A in @tbl-sdm-offsets is a ratio because that fit is on the log scale.

Every response-surface run cleared leached Protein A by more than the platform worst case of `{python} num(LPA_PF)` on which the Protein A criterion relies. Leached Protein A is not a response of the designs, so no model replaces that platform value (@sec-verification).

@tbl-flow gives the results of the flow-rate study at both ends of the range, with the qualification runs at the set-point as the reference. Aggregate and host cell protein are stated at manufacturing scale. Every result at both ends met its criterion, so the range studied of `{python} prng('flow', 'range')` is supported for aggregate and host cell protein by its own data. Fragments were not measured, so the study supports no range for fragments.

For aggregate and host cell protein the differences between the ends, `{python} num(FLOW['aggregate_out_pct']['raw'])` percentage points and `{python} num(FLOW['hcp_out_ng_mg']['raw'])` ng/mg in the scale-down model, are smaller than the smallest effect found significant in the screening design, `{python} num(SIG_MIN['aggregate_out_pct'])` points and `{python} num(SIG_MIN['hcp_out_ng_mg'])` ng/mg. For step yield the interval of the difference, `{python} num(100 * FLOW['step_yield']['lo'])` to `{python} num(100 * FLOW['step_yield']['hi'])` points, is wide enough to include an effect as large as that of protein load in the screening design (`{python} num(-100 * SIG_MIN['step_yield'])` points). The study is too small to exclude such an effect on yield.

```{python}
T.frame(_fc, "Elution flow rate, the high end of the range against the low end.", "tbl-flow-cmp",
```

Residual DNA clearance was `{python} f"{-FLOW['dna_lrv']['diff']:.2f}"` log10 lower at the high end than at the low end (95 % CI `{python} f"{-FLOW['dna_lrv']['hi']:.2f}"` to `{python} f"{-FLOW['dna_lrv']['lo']:.2f}"` log10 lower, `{python} pq(FLOW['dna_lrv']['p'])`). It is the only response of the study for which the comparison reaches p < `{python} f"{ALPHA:g}"`. It rests on two runs at each end, and the lowest clearance, `{python} f"{DNA_LRV_UNI_MIN:.2f}"` log10 at `{python} pset('flow', UNI_LV[1])`, lies below the range of the response-surface runs. Residual DNA was not measured in the screening design, so there is no screening effect to set this difference against. With the scatter of the duplicates alone, the DNA comparison would not reach significance (`{python} pq(FLOW['dna_lrv']['p_dup'])`) and the yield comparison would (`{python} pq(FLOW['step_yield']['p_dup'])`). That estimate of the scatter rests on two pairs of runs. It is larger than the residual SD of the response-surface design for aggregate and residual DNA clearance, and smaller for host cell protein and step yield. Both pools at the high end carried leached Protein A below the LOQ, so its clearance there is known only as a lower bound.

The study detected no effect of flow rate on aggregate or host cell protein comparable in size with the effects of the screening design. It detected none on yield, but it cannot exclude one as large as the effect of protein load. Flow rate was not carried into a multivariate study. Residual DNA clearance was significantly lower at the high end of the flow-rate range. Residual DNA has no criterion at this step, and @sec-classification judges the practical relevance of the difference against the drug substance.

## Mechanistic interpretation {#sec-mechanism}

Protein load and elution buffer pH acted on aggregate in the directions expected. A higher load occupies more of the ligand and broadens the elution peaks, so the aggregate front overlaps more of the monomer. A higher pH lowers the positive charge of both species, which weakens their binding and brings them off closer together. The positive load × pH interaction fits the same picture, since the separation that load erodes is the separation that a high pH has already compressed. Within this range conductivity has no demonstrated effect on aggregate, as expected. The ionic strength of the load and the wash weakens the binding of every species during loading and washing. It does not change the relative charge of aggregate and monomer at the elution pH, which is what separates them.

The elution stop collect acted on aggregate in the opposite direction to the expectation of PCP-007 §4.1. A higher setting stops collection earlier on the descending edge and should leave more of the aggregate tail out of the pool. In both designs aggregate instead rose as the setting rose, by `{python} f"{fold_lh('aggregate_out_pct', 'stop_collect'):.2f}"`-fold across the range in the response-surface model, with its lowest value near `{python} f"{STOP_MIN:.2f}"` AU. The selected yield model has no stop collect term, where a later stop was expected to recover more monomer (@sec-rsm-yield). The mechanism of @sec-platform does not explain these results, and this report gives no cause for them.

Protein load and load/wash conductivity acted on host cell protein in the directions expected. More load leaves more host cell protein held with the bound antibody, and a higher ionic strength strips more of the weakly bound species in the wash. On the log scale each acts as a constant factor, so in ng/mg conductivity removes more host cell protein at a high load, where there is more to remove, as the plan expected. A change with load of the share that conductivity removes was not found. The pH × conductivity interaction was not expected, and the mechanism of @sec-platform does not explain it.

Residual DNA clearance did not depend on any of the four factors of the response-surface design, as expected for a species repelled by the ligand. The lower clearance at the highest flow rate is not explained by that mechanism either. Leached Protein A was cleared by a modest factor, as expected for a species partly bound in complex with the antibody. Yield fell with load, as expected when broader peaks lose more monomer at their edges.

# Design space {#sec-ds}

The design space of the step is the region of its four multivariate parameters, within their ranges studied, over which every output with a criterion meets it at both ends of the `{python} PI_PCT` % prediction interval of a single run (PCMP-001 §6.2, PCP-007 §7.5). Aggregate and host cell protein enter through their selected models, at manufacturing scale. Fragments have no adequate model and no measured offset. They constrain the region through their measured results in the scale-down model, all of which met the criterion. On the grid of `{python} f"{N_GRID:,}"` points, `{python} f"{100 * DSG['fraction']:.0f}"` % of the region meets every criterion in force. The region drawn on the mean prediction, for comparison, is also the whole region (`{python} f"{100 * DSG_MEAN['fraction']:.0f}"` %).

That result rests on the widening of the host cell protein criterion (@sec-basis). At the a priori criterion of `{python} C_HCP_AP` ng/mg, `{python} f"{100 * DS_AP:.2f}"` % of the grid would meet every criterion. The `{python} N_AP_OUT` points outside lie at `{python} pset('load', PR['load'][1])`, `{python} pset('wash_cond', PR['wash_cond'][0])` and elution buffer pH `{python} f"{AP_PH_MIN:g}"` and above, with single-run limits up to `{python} num(AP_MAX)` ng/mg.

No attribute bounds the region within the ranges studied. Host cell protein comes nearest to its criterion. Its highest single-run limit over the region is `{python} num(CUBE_UP['hcp_out_ng_mg'][0])` ng/mg at `{python} corner(CUBE_UP['hcp_out_ng_mg'][1], HCP_FAC)`, at any stop collect setting, `{python} num(ACC['hcp_out_ng_mg'][1] - CUBE_UP['hcp_out_ng_mg'][0])` ng/mg below the criterion. The highest single-run limit of aggregate is `{python} num(CUBE_UP['aggregate_out_pct'][0])` % at `{python} corner(CUBE_UP['aggregate_out_pct'][1])`, against `{python} C_AGG` %. The NOR lies inside the ranges studied for every parameter, and inside the design space.

Four results bound this claim near the corner of highest load and lowest conductivity. Screening run `{python} S9_RUN` at such a corner gave host cell protein above the criterion (@sec-screening). Of the other host cell protein models within `{python} f"{DAICC:g}"` AICc units of the selected one, `{python} len(HCP_ALT_OUT)` put a small part of that corner outside the criterion (@sec-near). At that corner each design has a single run, and the two runs differ by a factor of `{python} f"{HCP_SR_MAXF:.1f}"`. With the run-order drift of host cell protein added, `{python} f"{100 * DS_DRIFT_OUT:.2f}"` % of the grid would exceed the criterion (@sec-rsm-hcp). The design space has not been confirmed at manufacturing scale anywhere near the edges of the ranges studied. The claim also holds only at the set-point of elution flow rate, which is not a factor of the designs, and only within the qualified life of the resin.

Under ICH Q8(R2), working within an approved design space does not need a regulatory change [@ichq8]. Any planned movement is still assessed under the change management of the quality system [@ichq10]. The NOR of this step was not changed, and the plan's rule that a range is not narrowed to make a margin the data do not require applies (PCP-007 §7.5).

# Proven acceptable ranges {#sec-par}

## Acceptance basis {#sec-basis}

Each output is judged against its intermediate acceptance criterion (PCMP-001 §7.3). The rule carries each drug substance criterion backward through the train, using the worst case that each later step showed on the platform for X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab, and applies no margin. @tbl-iac gives the derivation for this step. The derivation of the a priori criteria uses no result of the studies they judge.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.iac_derivation(["cex"]).show()
```

No later step changes fragments in the derivation, so the pool is judged against the drug substance criterion of `{python} C_FRAG` % for fragments. No later step removes aggregate. PCMP-001 assumed that none adds any either, so the a priori aggregate criterion of the pool was the drug substance criterion of `{python} C_AGG_AP` %. UF/DF raises aggregate within its NOR. The UF/DF report PCR-010 gives the one-sided `{python} VB_PCT` % prediction bound of a single run for that rise, `{python} f"{UFDF_ADD:.3f}"` percentage points, with the offset of its scale-down model applied. Carried back from the drug substance criterion, that bound tightens the criterion of this pool to `{python} C_AGG` %. The tightening changes no conclusion of this report, because the highest single-run limit of aggregate over the NOR, `{python} num(UPL['aggregate_out_pct'])` %, meets both values. For host cell protein the drug substance criterion of `{python} num(CQA.loc['hcp', 'acc_high'])` ng/mg is carried back through anion exchange. With the platform worst case of anion exchange, a clearance factor of `{python} num(VAEX['assumed'])`, the criterion is `{python} C_HCP_AP` ng/mg a priori. The anion exchange report PCR-008 verified that worst case, and the one-sided `{python} VB_PCT` % prediction bound of a single batch at the least favourable combination of its NOR, `{python} f"{HCP_DSF:.2f}"`, replaced it. The criterion in force is therefore `{python} C_HCP` ng/mg.

That widening is argued here by its risk, in the four parts of PCMP-001 §7.5.

1. Who bears the risk. A wider criterion lets the pool of this step carry up to `{python} C_HCP` ng/mg into anion exchange instead of `{python} C_HCP_AP` ng/mg. If anion exchange then cleared only its platform worst case, the drug substance could carry `{python} num(ACC['hcp_out_ng_mg'][1] / VAEX['assumed'])` ng/mg, above its criterion. The risk falls on the producer where such a result is detected, and on the patient only where it is not.
2. Detection. Host cell protein is a release test of the drug substance, by the ELISA AMV-3012 with an LOQ of `{python} num(METH.loc['AMV-3012', 'loq'])` ng/mg. Its reagent covers `{python} f"{float(METH.loc['AMV-3012', 'coverage_pct']):g}"` % of the host cell proteins seen by `{python} METH.loc['AMV-3012', 'coverage_method']`, so an excursion made only of the species outside that coverage would not be detected.
3. What the later steps must clear. Anion exchange must clear `{python} f"{HCP_DSF:.2f}"`-fold to bring the criterion in force to the drug substance criterion, which is its bound. The bound in force comes from the `{python} N_AEX_RSM` planned runs of its response-surface design, on a model that meets the first three adequacy criteria (R² minus predicted R² `{python} f"{VAEX['r2_minus_pred_r2']:.3f}"`, lack of fit `{python} pq(VAEX['p_lack_of_fit'])`). On all `{python} N_AEX_RSM + N_AEX_AUG` of its runs, with the `{python} N_AEX_AUG` runs of the INV-002 augmentation, the bound is also `{python} f"{VAEX_ALL['predicted_nor_bound95']:.2f}"`. The bound holds within the NOR of anion exchange. At the edges of its range studied the lowest clearance factor measured was `{python} num(VAEX['observed_edge'])`, below the platform value.
4. The drug substance. No simulated batch of the integrated model exceeded the host cell protein criterion of the drug substance, so the probability is below `{python} f"{100 * P_UB:.2f}"` % (@sec-capability).

The widening changes no conclusion of this report over the NOR. The highest single-run limit of the pool over the NOR, `{python} num(UPL['hcp_out_ng_mg'])` ng/mg, meets the a priori criterion as well. The widening does decide two results outside that judgement. At the a priori criterion the scale-down model would not be qualified for host cell protein (@sec-sdm), and the design space would cover `{python} f"{100 * DS_AP:.2f}"` % of the region studied instead of all of it (@sec-ds). The proven acceptable ranges would not change.

Residual DNA, leached Protein A and step yield have no criterion at this step, so no range is derived from them. The platform history gives no worst-case DNA clearance for the steps after Protein A, so no DNA criterion can be carried back, and residual DNA is judged on the drug substance only (PCMP-001 §7.3). Leached Protein A is judged in the Protein A pool, against a criterion of `{python} num(UP_PA_LPA['iac_high'])` ppm carried back through the platform worst cases of cation exchange and anion exchange.

Aggregate has a median of `{python} num(AG_SP)` % at the set-point, and its single-run limits over the NOR run from `{python} num(LOL['aggregate_out_pct'])` % to `{python} num(UPL['aggregate_out_pct'])` %. The least favourable combination is `{python} corner(WC['aggregate_out_pct']['settings'])`. ## Proven acceptable ranges per parameter {#sec-par-table}

The set-point analysis gives the range of one parameter with the rest of the step at target. The NOR-propagated analysis gives the range over which the `{python} f"{PI_UP:g}"`th percentile of simulated single batches meets the criterion while the other factors vary within their NORs, and it is the range that supports a claim (@sec-statistics). @tbl-par gives both for aggregate and host cell protein. Every range is the range studied, so each proven acceptable range reaches the edge of the characterized range and no claim is made beyond it (PCMP-001 §7.6).
