For elution flow rate, the range of `{python} prng('flow', 'range')` is supported by its own data for aggregate and host cell protein (@sec-flow).

## Verification of the platform worst cases {#sec-verification}

The criteria upstream of this step assume that cation exchange clears each attribute at least as well as its platform worst case. @tbl-iac-verification sets each platform worst case against this campaign's results.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.worst_case_verification(["cex"]).show()
```

Aggregate. Within its NOR the step cleared aggregate less than the platform worst case of `{python} num(VER.loc['aggregates_hmw', 'assumed'])`. At manufacturing scale the lowest clearance factor predicted was `{python} num(VER.loc['aggregates_hmw', 'predicted_nor'])`, at the combination of `{python} corner(WC['aggregate_out_pct']['settings'])`. By rule 1 of PCMP-001 §7.5 the one-sided `{python} VB_PCT` % prediction bound of a single batch there, `{python} num(VER.loc['aggregates_hmw', 'predicted_nor_bound95'])`, replaced the platform value, and the aggregate criteria upstream became stricter. The criterion of the low-pH pool moved from `{python} num(UP_VI['iac_high_apriori'])` % to `{python} num(UP_VI['iac_high'])` %. The criterion of the bioreactor harvest moved from `{python} num(UP_BRX['iac_high_apriori'])` % to `{python} num(UP_BRX['iac_high'])` %, a value that also includes a widening from the low-pH step (PCR-006). The bound comes from the `{python} N_RSM` runs of the response-surface design, on a model that meets all four adequacy criteria. At the edges of the range studied the step cleared less still, `{python} num(VER.loc['aggregates_hmw', 'observed_edge'])` at the lowest, outside the NOR. With each flagged run deleted the lowest predicted factor stays below the platform value and the bound lies between `{python} num(min(AGG_DEL_BOUNDS))` and `{python} num(max(AGG_DEL_BOUNDS))` (@tbl-deletion). The plan's full quadratic would have given a bound of `{python} num(VFULL_AGG['predicted_nor_bound95'])`.

That tightening is argued by its risk, in the four parts of PCMP-001 §7.5.

1. Who bears the risk. A stricter criterion lowers the aggregate that the low-pH pool and the harvest may carry. It lowers the patient's risk and raises the producer's, because a pool between the new and the a priori criterion now fails.
2. Detection. No step after cation exchange removes aggregate, so the aggregate of this pool reaches the drug substance with the small rise across UF/DF. There it is a release test by SEC. An excursion of a pool upstream beyond its tightened criterion would therefore be detected at release whenever it carried the drug substance above `{python} C_AGG_AP` %.
3. What the later steps must clear. Cation exchange must clear `{python} num(VER.loc['aggregates_hmw', 'predicted_nor_bound95'])`-fold from the criterion of the low-pH pool to the criterion of its own pool, `{python} C_AGG` %, which is its own bound within the NOR. UF/DF may then add up to `{python} f"{UFDF_ADD:.3f}"` percentage points, which brings the pool to the drug substance criterion. No later step is credited with any clearance of aggregate.
4. The drug substance. No simulated batch exceeded the aggregate criterion of the drug substance, so the probability is below `{python} f"{100 * P_UB:.2f}"` %, and the capability index is `{python} f"{CAPR.loc['aggregates_hmw', 'Cpk']:.1f}"` (@sec-capability).

Two studies of the low-pH viral inactivation report ran this step at its set-point on material from the low-pH step, after the criteria were fixed. They tested whether cation exchange clears aggregate and fragments by the factors the criteria rely on, `{python} num(VER.loc['aggregates_hmw', 'predicted_nor_bound95'])` and `{python} num(VER.loc['fragments_lmw', 'assumed'])`. In S-CEX-VER (discrepancy PD-006-02) and S-VI-WC (PD-006-03) every run cleared aggregate by `{python} num(AGGF_VER[0])` to `{python} num(AGGF_VER[-1])`-fold, and the lower confidence bound of each study met the factor required. For fragments, S-CEX-VER met its factor. In S-VI-WC every run cleared fragments by more than `{python} num(VER.loc['fragments_lmw', 'assumed'])`-fold, but the lower bound of the three runs did not, so the rule set before those runs was not met, and PCR-006 accepts the result on its risk. Both studies, their results and their decisions belong to PCR-006.

Host cell protein. At manufacturing scale the lowest clearance factor predicted within the NOR, `{python} num(VER.loc['hcp', 'predicted_nor'])`, is not below the platform worst case of `{python} num(VER.loc['hcp', 'assumed'])`, so the assumption is confirmed. The bound of a single batch, `{python} num(VER.loc['hcp', 'predicted_nor_bound95'])`, is not better than the platform value, so the platform value stands. At the edges of the range studied the lowest factor measured was `{python} num(VER.loc['hcp', 'observed_edge'])`, outside the NOR. The same outcome follows with each flagged run deleted. It does not follow under every model within `{python} f"{DAICC:g}"` AICc units of the selected one. Under `{python} len(HCP_ALT_NC)` of the `{python} len(NEAR_ALT['hcp_out_ng_mg'])` other models the lowest factor falls below the platform value (@sec-near).

The verification converts the scale-down prediction to manufacturing scale with the offset at its estimate (PCMP-001 §7.1 rule 2). Its outcome for host cell protein depends on that estimate. With the offset at the unfavourable end of its interval the lowest factor would be `{python} num(VER_END['hcp']['lo'])` and the bound `{python} num(VERB_END['hcp']['lo'])`, and rule 1 of PCMP-001 §7.5 would then have tightened the host cell protein criterion of the Protein A pool. With the offset at the favourable end the lowest factor would be `{python} num(VER_END['hcp']['hi'])` and the bound `{python} num(VERB_END['hcp']['hi'])`, better than the platform value. For aggregate the outcome is the same at either end of its interval, with lowest factors of `{python} num(VER_END['aggregates_hmw']['lo'])` and `{python} num(VER_END['aggregates_hmw']['hi'])`.

Fragments. The lowest clearance factor that the fragment model predicts within the NOR, `{python} num(VER.loc['fragments_lmw', 'predicted_nor'])`, is not below the platform worst case of `{python} num(VER.loc['fragments_lmw', 'assumed'])`. By the rule of PCP-007 §7.6 the assumption is therefore confirmed, as @tbl-iac-verification shows. The bound of a single batch, `{python} num(VER.loc['fragments_lmw', 'predicted_nor_bound95'])`, is not better than the platform value, so the platform value stands. The fragment model behind this confirmation does not meet the limit on overfitting of PCMP-001 §7.2 (@sec-rsm-frag), and fragments have no measured offset, so the factor is the one the scale-down model gives. At the edges of the range studied the lowest clearance factor measured was `{python} num(VER.loc['fragments_lmw', 'observed_edge'])`, just below the platform value. The fragment criteria of the Protein A pool (`{python} num(UP_PA_FRAG['iac_high'])` %) and the low-pH pool (`{python} num(UP_VI_FRAG['iac_high'])` %) rely on this value.

Leached Protein A. Leached Protein A is not a response of the designs, so its platform value of `{python} num(LPA_PF)` stands without verification by a model. Every response-surface run cleared more than that factor (@sec-dna-lpa).

# Process capability and robustness {#sec-capability}

Capability is estimated for the drug substance from the integrated model of the train (PCMP-001 §6.5). The capability of the step itself, which PCP-007 §5.5 asked for, was not estimated (@sec-statistics). @tbl-cap gives the capability index of each drug substance attribute that this step clears, from `{python} f"{NMC:,}"` simulated batches with every parameter drawn within its NOR.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_lab_cap = {"aggregates_hmw": T.ATTR_NAME["aggregates_hmw"], "hcp": T.ATTR_NAME["hcp"],
            "fragments_lmw": T.ATTR_NAME["fragments_lmw"], "residual_dna": "Residual DNA (ng/dose)",
            "leached_protein_a": T.ATTR_NAME["leached_protein_a"]}
_cp = pd.DataFrame({"Attribute": [_lab_cap[k] for k in CAPK],
                    "Criticality": [CQA.loc[k, "criticality"] for k in CAPK],
                    "Criterion": [crit(0.0, float(CQA.loc[k, "acc_high"]), "upper") if k != "residual_dna"
                                  else f"≤ {float(CQA.loc[k, 'acc_high']):g}" for k in CAPK],
                    "Mean ± SD": [msd(k) for k in CAPK],
                    "Cpk": [f"{CAPR.loc[k, 'Cpk']:.2f}" if CAPR.loc[k, "Cpk"] < 100 else f"{CAPR.loc[k, 'Cpk']:,.0f}" for k in CAPK],
                    "Batches outside": [str(int(POOS.loc[k, "n_oos"])) for k in CAPK]})
T.frame(_cp, "Capability of the drug substance attributes that cation exchange clears.", "tbl-cap",
        header={"Criterion": "Drug substance\ncriterion", "Batches outside": "Simulated batches\noutside"},
        align=["P{3.6cm}", "c", "l", "r", "r", "r"],
        notes=[("", f"One-sided index against the upper criterion. Mean and SD of {NMC:,} simulated batches of the integrated model, in the unit of the criterion. Residual DNA in ng per dose.")],
        notes_per_row=True).show()
```

Every index exceeds the target of `{python} CPK_TARGET`, and none approaches the minimum of `{python} CPK_MIN`. Host cell protein has the lowest index, `{python} f"{CAPR.loc['hcp', 'Cpk']:.2f}"`, with a mean of `{python} num(MCM['hcp'])` ng/mg against `{python} num(CQA.loc['hcp', 'acc_high'])` ng/mg. No simulated batch fell outside any of the five criteria. With `{python} f"{NMC:,}"` batches that bounds the probability of an out of specification result for each attribute below `{python} f"{100 * P_UB:.2f}"` % at one-sided 95 % confidence. The bound covers the sampling of the simulation and not the uncertainty of the integrated model itself.

The index of leached Protein A, `{python} f"{CAPR.loc['leached_protein_a', 'Cpk']:,.0f}"`, is not meaningful, because the simulated mean of `{python} f"{MCM['leached_protein_a']:.4f}"` ppm lies far below the criterion of `{python} num(CQA.loc['leached_protein_a', 'acc_high'])` ppm. Leached Protein A is judged instead by the criterion of the Protein A pool and the clearance of the steps after it. Residual DNA is judged per dose. The dose is A-Mab's `{python} f"{DOSE['mg_per_kg']:g}"` mg/kg, `{python} f"{DOSE_MG:g}"` mg for a reference adult of `{python} f"{DOSE['body_weight_kg']:g}"` kg, and the body weight is an assumption of this campaign. The simulated drug substance carries `{python} f"{MCM['residual_dna']:.5f}"` ng per dose on average against `{python} f"{CQA.loc['residual_dna', 'acc_high']:g}"` ng. That result depends on inputs from outside this step's data, the DNA clearance that the process model credits to this step (`{python} f"{DNA_LRV_PROC:g}"` log10) and to anion exchange (`{python} f"{DNA_LRV_AEX:g}"` log10). The pool of this step alone carried up to `{python} num(RSM.dna_pool_pg_mg.max())` pg/mg in the response-surface runs, `{python} num(dna_ng_per_dose(RSM.dna_pool_pg_mg.max()))` ng per dose, so the drug substance criterion is met through anion exchange.

The derivation of the criteria credits no later step with removing aggregate, so the aggregate of the drug substance is the aggregate of this pool plus the small rise across UF/DF. It shares the clearance of host cell protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A with anion exchange. The robustness of the step within its NOR is shown by the margins of @sec-criteria-results, and its least margin lies at corners outside the NOR (@sec-ds).

# Parameter classification {#sec-classification}

Parameters were classified under SOP-4001 by the decision logic of the A-Mab case study [@amab2009], as PCMP-001 §7.7 sets it out. A critical process parameter "has an effect on a CQA that is significant and practically relevant within the characterized range, and a high risk of falling outside its acceptable range in operation". A well-controlled critical process parameter "has the same kind of effect on a CQA but a low risk of falling outside its acceptable range, because it is readily controlled and its PAR is wide against its NOR". A key process parameter affects process performance and has no effect on a CQA within its range. A general process parameter "has no relevant effect on a CQA or on process performance within its range". PCMP-001 §7.7 adds that "a significant effect that is too small to move the attribute appreciably within the PAR does not by itself make a parameter critical". An attribute is called affected by a parameter when a term that contains the parameter is significant at α = `{python} f"{ALPHA:g}"` (PCMP-001 §6.2). No numerical threshold is set for practical relevance or for a PAR that is wide against its NOR. Each class below is therefore stated with the size of the effect across the proven acceptable range and the margin of that range to the NOR.

- Protein load was classified as a WC-CPP. It affects aggregate, through its main effect and its interactions with pH and stop collect, and host cell protein, through its main effect. With the other factors at their set-points, aggregate rises from `{python} num(AG_L[0])` % to `{python} num(AG_L[1])` % and host cell protein from `{python} num(HC_L[0])` to `{python} num(HC_L[2])` ng/mg across the range of `{python} prng('load', 'range')`. Its proven acceptable range is the range studied, `{python} f"{MARG['load']:g}"` g/L resin beyond each end of its NOR, and the load is set by the mass of antibody applied per litre of resin.
- Load/wash conductivity was classified as a WC-CPP. It affects host cell protein, through its main effect and its interaction with pH, and has no demonstrated effect on aggregate. Host cell protein falls from `{python} num(HC_W[0])` to `{python} num(HC_W[1])` ng/mg across `{python} prng('wash_cond', 'range')`. Its proven acceptable range is the range studied, `{python} f"{MARG['wash_cond']:g}"` mS/cm beyond each end of its NOR.
- Elution buffer pH was classified as a WC-CPP. It affects aggregate, through its main effect and its interactions with load and stop collect, and host cell protein through its interaction with conductivity. Aggregate rises from `{python} num(AG_P[0])` % to `{python} num(AG_P[1])` % across `{python} prng('elution_ph', 'range')`. Its proven acceptable range is the range studied, `{python} f"{MARG['elution_ph']:g}"` pH units beyond each end of its NOR, the narrowest margin of the four.
- Elution stop collect was classified as a WC-CPP. It affects aggregate, through its main effect, its curvature and its interactions with load and pH, in the direction opposite to the expectation (@sec-mechanism). Aggregate is `{python} num(AG_S[0])` %, `{python} num(AG_S[1])` % and `{python} num(AG_S[2])` % at settings of `{python} pset('stop_collect', PR['stop_collect'][0])`, `{python} pset('stop_collect', SP['stop_collect'])` and `{python} pset('stop_collect', PR['stop_collect'][1])`. Its proven acceptable range is the range studied, `{python} f"{MARG['stop_collect']:g}"` AU beyond each end of its NOR.
- Elution flow rate was classified as a GPP. The class rests on a judgement of practical relevance, for which no plan sets a threshold. Its range studied of `{python} prng('flow', 'range')` extends `{python} f"{MARG_FLOW:g}"` cm/hr beyond each end of its NOR. No difference was detected in aggregate or host cell protein, and every result met its criterion (@sec-flow). Residual DNA clearance was `{python} f"{-FLOW['dna_lrv']['diff']:.2f}"` log10 lower at `{python} pset('flow', UNI_LV[1])` than at `{python} pset('flow', UNI_LV[0])` (`{python} pq(FLOW['dna_lrv']['p'])`), so under PCMP-001 §6.2 residual DNA is affected by flow rate. The difference is a factor of `{python} f"{DNA_FLOW_F:.1f}"` in the residual DNA of the pool across the range studied, and about `{python} f"{DNA_FLOW_F_NOR:.2f}"` across the NOR if the effect is linear in flow rate. The drug substance carries `{python} f"{MCM['residual_dna']:.5f}"` ng per dose on average against a criterion of `{python} f"{CQA.loc['residual_dna', 'acc_high']:g}"` ng, with a capability index of `{python} f"{CAPR.loc['residual_dna', 'Cpk']:.2f}"` (@sec-capability). If the whole factor reached the drug substance, its mean would be `{python} f"{DNA_DS_AT_F:.5f}"` ng per dose and its capability index `{python} f"{CPK_DNA_AT_F:.2f}"`, still above the target of `{python} CPK_TARGET`. This report therefore judges the effect too small to move residual DNA appreciably in the drug substance, in the sense of PCMP-001 §7.7. For step yield the study detected no difference, but the interval of the difference, `{python} num(100 * FLOW['step_yield']['lo'])` to `{python} num(100 * FLOW['step_yield']['hi'])` points, includes an effect as large as that of protein load (`{python} num(100 * Y_LOAD_EFF)` points). The study therefore does not show that flow rate leaves yield unchanged. For yield the class rests on the absence of a detected difference and on the expectation of PCP-007 §4.1 that flow rate, within its range, changes the sharpness of the elution peak only a little. Fragments were not measured in the flow-rate study, so for fragments the class rests on the mechanism alone. Flow rate changes the residence time and the mass transfer in the resin, and it changes neither the charge of the antibody nor the ionic strength that holds it.

Of the `{python} N_PAR` parameters, `{python} N_WC` are critical process parameters, all of them well controlled, and one is a general process parameter. Each WC-CPP has a proven acceptable range equal to its range studied, and the conclusions over the NOR hold with margin for each attribute with a criterion.

# Contribution to the control strategy {#sec-control}

The step contributes four elements to the control strategy of the drug substance. The results of this report roll up, with those of the other steps, into the master report PCMR-001.

1. Parameter ranges. The four WC-CPPs are controlled within their NORs, which lie inside proven acceptable ranges equal to the ranges studied and inside a design space that covers the whole region studied at the criteria in force (@sec-ds and @sec-par-table). Elution flow rate is controlled within its NOR as a GPP.
2. Criteria for the steps upstream. The verification of this report tightened the aggregate criteria of the low-pH pool and the bioreactor harvest, which PCR-006 and PCR-003 judge. The host cell protein criterion of the Protein A pool, `{python} num(UP_PA_HCP['iac_high'])` ng/mg, assumes the platform clearance of this step, which this report confirmed with the offset at its estimate (@sec-verification).
3. The criteria this step hands on. The pool must meet `{python} C_HCP` ng/mg of host cell protein for anion exchange to bring it to the drug substance criterion. It must meet `{python} C_AGG` % of aggregate so that the rise across UF/DF keeps the drug substance within its criterion. It meets both across the NOR, with highest single-run limits of `{python} num(UPL['hcp_out_ng_mg'])` ng/mg and `{python} num(UPL['aggregate_out_pct'])` %.
4. Release testing. The drug substance criteria of @tbl-cqas apply at release. For aggregate and fragments the register names the method, SEC and nrCE-SDS.

This report proposes no in-process control or monitoring of the pool beyond these four elements.

The conclusions of this report hold for resin within the cycle count qualified under SOP-2008. Cation exchange claims no viral clearance. Low-pH viral inactivation inactivates enveloped virus (PCR-006). Anion exchange clears host cell protein, residual DNA, leached Protein A and virus after this step (PCR-008). Virus filtration removes virus (PCR-009).

# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

A higher protein load and a higher elution buffer pH raise aggregate in the pool. More load broadens the elution peaks, so that aggregate overlaps more of the monomer. A higher pH lowers the positive charge that holds both species, so that they come off closer together. A higher protein load also raises host cell protein, because more of it is held with the bound antibody. A higher load/wash conductivity lowers host cell protein, because a higher ionic strength strips more of the weakly bound species in the wash, and elution buffer pH changes the size of that effect. A higher stop collect setting raises aggregate, against the expected mechanism. The selected yield model has no stop collect term, where a later stop was expected to recover more monomer. Neither result is explained.

Confidence in the scale-down model rests on the offsets of @tbl-sdm-offsets. For aggregate the offset is close to 1 and well determined. For host cell protein the ratio is known only to within its interval of `{python} f"{OFF['hcp_out_ng_mg']['lo']:.2f}"` to `{python} f"{OFF['hcp_out_ng_mg']['hi']:.2f}"`. The model is qualified for host cell protein at the criterion in force. It would not be qualified at the a priori criterion, under `{python} len(HCP_ALT_UNQ)` of the other models within `{python} f"{DAICC:g}"` AICc units of the selected one, or with the run-order drift added at the unfavourable end of the offset interval (@sec-sdm, @sec-near and @sec-rsm-hcp).

Screening run `{python} RUN6` was made with the expired buffer lot. With it deleted, the screening models find the same significant terms. Response-surface run `{python} RUN14` had the temperature excursion. With it deleted, the judgement over the NOR, the design space and the outcome of the verification are unchanged (@sec-record). Deleting run `{python} RUN14` does change two selected models. The aggregate model loses its conductivity term, and the yield model replaces its `{python} tname(Y14_DROP[0])` interaction with a stop collect term.

The discrepancies from the plan fall into three groups. The analysis departs from the plan in the model selection, in the use of a host cell protein model that does not meet the residual criterion, and in the approaches taken where the plan sets no threshold. The selection changed the terms of the models but no conclusion over the NOR. The run-order drift of the host cell protein residuals, a factor of `{python} f"{HCP_DRIFT_F:.2f}"` over the study, would raise the highest single-run limit over the NOR to `{python} num(HCP_UPL_DRIFT)` ng/mg, below the criterion of `{python} C_HCP` ng/mg. The execution departs from the plan in the flow-rate study without its set-point run, the residual DNA offset recorded without investigation, and the fractionated runs of S-CEX-FRC. The record lacks the load results, the residual DNA and leached Protein A results of the screening runs, the fractions and the mass balance, the packing tests of each campaign and the feed lots. The missing load results matter most, because every clearance factor of aggregate and host cell protein rests on the process model at set-point instead of a measured load. Apart from these groups, discrepancy PD-007-12 corrects the name of the load/wash buffer of screening run `{python} RUN6` and changes no result.

Five limitations remain.

1. Scale. The scale-down model does not reproduce the hold times, pool volumes or mixing of the commercial suite, and no run at manufacturing scale tests the edges of the design space. The process performance qualification (PPQ) batches of Stage 2, which have not yet been run, test the step at its set-points.
2. The corner of highest load and lowest conductivity. One screening result there exceeded the host cell protein criterion, and the edge of the design space at that corner depends on the choice among the models within `{python} f"{DAICC:g}"` AICc units of the selected one and on the run-order drift. The corner lies outside the NOR of every parameter.
3. The size of the flow-rate study. With two runs at each end and no set-point run, the study cannot exclude an effect on yield as large as that of load, and its significant difference in DNA clearance rests on four runs.
4. Fragments. Fragments have no adequate model and no offset. Their judgement rests on measured results in the scale-down model and on the assumption that they separate alike at both scales, and the confirmation of their platform worst case rests on the inadequate model.
5. Resin life cycle. The conclusions hold within the qualified life of the resin, and performance at the end of that life is established by the life-cycle study under SOP-2008, not here.

# Conclusions {#sec-conclusions}

1. Objective 1 is met. The relationships between the four multivariate parameters and the outputs of the step were quantified over ranges wider than the NORs. Protein load, elution buffer pH and elution stop collect affect aggregate, and protein load and load/wash conductivity affect host cell protein, with pH acting through conductivity. The stop collect acts on aggregate in the direction opposite to the expectation.
2. Objective 2 is met for aggregate and host cell protein and not met for fragments. The design space is drawn on the single-run limit, at manufacturing scale, for aggregate and host cell protein. At the criteria in force it covers the whole region studied, and at the a priori host cell protein criterion it would cover `{python} f"{100 * DS_AP:.2f}"` %. Host cell protein comes nearest to its criterion, at a corner outside the NOR. Fragments have no adequate model, so no model predicts where they meet their criterion. Their measured results, all below the criterion, constrain the region instead.
3. Objective 3 is met for aggregate and host cell protein and not met for fragments. Every output meets its intermediate acceptance criterion across the NOR. The highest single-run limits are `{python} num(UPL['aggregate_out_pct'])` % for aggregate and `{python} num(UPL['hcp_out_ng_mg'])` ng/mg for host cell protein, and fragments were `{python} num(FRAG_MEAS.max())` % at most. Every proven acceptable range of aggregate and host cell protein is the range studied. Fragments have no adequate model and therefore no proven acceptable range.
4. Objective 4 is met. The four multivariate parameters were classified as WC-CPPs and elution flow rate as a GPP, the latter by a judgement of the practical relevance of its effect on residual DNA.
5. Objective 5 is met. The step contributes its parameter ranges, the criteria it sets for the steps upstream and the criteria it hands on to the control strategy. No in-process control or monitoring of the pool is proposed beyond these. The capability indices of the drug substance attributes it clears exceed `{python} CPK_TARGET`, the lowest `{python} f"{CAPR.loc['hcp', 'Cpk']:.2f}"` for host cell protein.
6. Objective 6 is met. The platform worst case for aggregate was not confirmed, and its bound of `{python} num(VER.loc['aggregates_hmw', 'predicted_nor_bound95'])` tightened the aggregate criteria upstream. The worst case for host cell protein was confirmed with the offset at its estimate and would not be at the unfavourable end of its interval. The worst case for fragments was confirmed by the rule of PCP-007 §7.6, because the lowest clearance factor predicted within the NOR is not below it, but on a model that does not meet PCMP-001 §7.2. The worst case for leached Protein A stands without verification by a model.
7. The runs of both study events were retained. Without screening run `{python} RUN6`, made with the expired buffer lot, the screening models find the same significant terms. Without response-surface run `{python} RUN14`, made during the temperature excursion, the judgement over the NOR, the design space and the outcome of the verification are unchanged, while the selected models of aggregate and yield change terms. The register records `{python} N_PD` discrepancies from the plan.

# Study events and discrepancies from the plan {#sec-record}

A process characterization study is not manufacture under good manufacturing practice, so it raises no deviation. The Version 1.0 plans called a departure from the plan a deviation. This report records two kinds of entry instead. Study events are the events of execution that Version 1.0 recorded, kept under the DEV numbers Version 1.0 gave them. Discrepancies from the plan are departures from the approved plan PCP-007, whether work the plan did not foresee or a requirement of the plan that was not met.

## Study events {#sec-events}

The studies of this step recorded `{python} N_DEV` study events, and the runs concerned were retained in the analysis.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(dev_register(DOC))
print()

```

### DEV-007-01 Expired buffer lot in a screening run {#sec-dev01}

The load/wash buffer used in screening run `{python} RUN6` came from lot `{python} LOT['id']`, which had expired on `{python} LOT['expiry']`, before the screening study started on `{python} CHR.loc['S-CEX-SCR', 'start']`. The lot is an acetate load/wash buffer, and Version 1.0 of this report named it a Tris buffer in error (discrepancy PD-007-12). The expiry was found in the documentation review after the study. The record gives the cause as an expiry date not checked at preparation. A lot that is within its expiry date when it is prepared can still be expired when it is used, so the check that would have found this lot is a check at the time of use. Under `{python} SOP2103['id']` (`{python} SOP2103['title']`), which authorises a re-test of the retained sample for an expired lot, the retained sample was re-tested and gave pH `{python} f"{dev_007_01_retest_ph:g}"` and a conductivity of `{python} f"{dev_007_01_retest_cond:g}"` mS/cm. That pH lies in the buffering range of acetate. The record gives no acceptance range for these values, so this report does not judge the lot from them.

The impact was judged from the data. Run `{python} RUN6` was made at `{python} corner(RUN6_SET)`. Its studentized residuals on the screening models were `{python} fm(RUN6_STUD['aggregate_out_pct'])` for aggregate, `{python} fm(RUN6_STUD['hcp_out_ng_mg'])` for host cell protein and `{python} fm(RUN6_STUD['step_yield'])` for step yield. With the run excluded, the screening models find the same significant terms for all three outputs. The screening design identifies effects and sets no range, so the run was retained.

### DEV-007-02 Temperature excursion during a response-surface run {#sec-dev02}

During response-surface run `{python} RUN14` the column inlet temperature was above its set-point for `{python} dev_007_02_duration` minutes and reached `{python} f"{dev_007_02_tmax:g}"` °C. The record gives neither the temperature set-point nor a permitted range. The excursion was found in the equipment history review of the chamber `{python} EQ.name`, and its cause was a drift of the set-point of the chamber controller. Temperature is not a factor of the designs. Aggregate in the pool of the run was verified by `{python} dev_007_02_ver_n` determinations by SEC under the method validation AMV-3221. At its precision of `{python} f"{float(METH.loc['AMV-3221', 'precision_pct']):g}"` % RSD, the mean of `{python} dev_007_02_ver_n` determinations has a 95 % confidence interval of ± `{python} f"{dev_007_02_ci_hw:g}"` % of its value. The record gives neither the result of these determinations nor a criterion they were judged against, so the verification decides nothing in this report. The impact of the run was judged from its residuals instead.

Run `{python} RUN14` was made at `{python} corner(RSM[RSM.run == RUN14].iloc[0])`. Its studentized residuals on the selected models were `{python} fm(RUN14_STUD['aggregate_out_pct'])` for aggregate, `{python} fm(RUN14_STUD['hcp_out_ng_mg'])` for host cell protein, `{python} fm(RUN14_STUD['lmw_cesds_pct'])` for fragments and `{python} fm(RUN14_STUD['step_yield'])` for step yield. With the run excluded and the selection repeated, the host cell protein model keeps the same terms and the aggregate model loses its conductivity main effect, which was not significant. Both outputs still meet their criteria over the NOR, with highest single-run limits of `{python} num(DEL14['aggregate_out_pct']['up_nor'])` % and `{python} num(DEL14['hcp_out_ng_mg']['up_nor'])` ng/mg, and the whole region studied still meets them. The lowest predicted clearance factor of aggregate stays below the platform value. The step yield model replaces its `{python} tname(Y14_DROP[0])` interaction with a stop collect term (@sec-rsm-yield), and yield has no criterion. The run was retained.

## Discrepancies from the plan {#sec-discrepancies}

@tbl-discrepancies lists the discrepancies from PCP-007.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(discrepancy_register(DOC))
print()
print(": Discrepancies from the plan PCP-007. {#tbl-discrepancies}")
```

### PD-007-01 Model selection {#sec-pd01}

PCP-007 prescribed the full quadratic model of each response-surface output. Each output was analysed instead by the model selection of INV-002 corrective action CA3 (@sec-statistics), because the full quadratic carries terms the data do not support. The selection changed the terms of every model and put aggregate and host cell protein on the log scale. It changed no conclusion over the NOR. With the plan's full quadratic, aggregate and host cell protein also meet their criteria over the NOR, and fragments fail the limit on overfitting under either analysis. Through the anion exchange model, the selection also widened the host cell protein criterion of this step from `{python} C_HCP_AP` to `{python} C_HCP` ng/mg. That widening decides the qualification of the scale-down model for host cell protein and whether the design space covers the whole region studied, and no conclusion over the NOR (@sec-basis). It also moved the bound that tightened the aggregate criteria upstream, from `{python} num(VFULL_AGG['predicted_nor_bound95'])` under the full quadratic to `{python} num(VER.loc['aggregates_hmw', 'predicted_nor_bound95'])`.

### PD-007-02 Conclusions on a model that does not meet the residual criterion {#sec-pd02}

PCP-007 required models that meet every adequacy criterion of PCMP-001 §7.2. The host cell protein model meets the first three and fails the fourth, because its residuals fall with the order of execution (`{python} pq(RIH['p_order'])`). It was used for the ranges and the design space. The trend amounts to a factor of `{python} f"{HCP_DRIFT_F:.2f}"` over the study, and added in full to the highest single-run limit over the NOR it gives `{python} num(HCP_UPL_DRIFT)` ng/mg against the criterion of `{python} C_HCP` ng/mg (@sec-rsm-hcp). No run of any model has a Cook's distance above the median of F(p, n − p), so no run fails the criterion. The flagged runs were each deleted and the selection repeated, which the plan provides, and no judgement over the NOR changed (@sec-influence). Outside the NOR the drift would move the edge of the design space and the qualification for host cell protein (@sec-rsm-hcp).

### PD-007-03 Flow-rate study without the set-point run {#sec-pd03}

PCP-007 §6.4 required the flow-rate study at the ends of the range and at the set-point. Each end was run in duplicate, and no run was made at the set-point. @tbl-flow shows the qualification runs at the set-point beside the flow-rate runs. They were made in a different study, before the characterization runs, so a difference between them and the flow-rate runs mixes any effect of flow rate with the variation between the two studies. The comparison of the two ends does not depend on them.

### PD-007-04 Residual DNA offset recorded, not investigated {#sec-pd04}

Version 1.0 of PCP-007 accepted the scale-down model only where no compared attribute differed significantly between the scales, and required the cause of a difference to be established before characterization went on. Residual DNA differed at that level (`{python} pq(P_V1['dna_pool_pg_mg'])`), and the difference was not investigated before the characterization runs. Under PCMP-001 Version 2.0 §7.1 a scale-down model may differ in mean from manufacturing scale where the offset is known precisely enough, so the Version 1.0 test was stricter than the use of the model needs (@sec-sdm).

### PD-007-05 Load aggregate and host cell protein not recorded {#sec-pd05}

PCP-007 §5.4 and §12 required aggregate and host cell protein to be measured in the load of every run, so that each output is read as a fold across the step and a clearance can be told apart from a low starting level. No load result for either attribute is in the record. Version 1.0 of this report stated that the load was assayed, with no result recorded. The clearance factors of this report are taken against the process model at set-point, which brings `{python} num(FEED_AGG)` % aggregate and `{python} f"{FEED_HCP:,.0f}"` ng/mg host cell protein to the step. The pool results and the judgements against the criteria do not depend on the load. The clearance factors and the verification of the platform worst cases do, and a load that differed from the process model between runs would appear in them as scatter or as a trend.

### PD-007-06 Residual DNA and leached Protein A not measured on the screening runs {#sec-pd06}

PCP-007 §5.4 required residual DNA and leached Protein A on every run of both designs. They were measured on the response-surface runs only. The analysis of both attributes rests on the `{python} N_RSM` response-surface runs (@sec-dna-lpa), and the flow-rate comparison of residual DNA has no screening effect to set against it (@sec-flow).

### PD-007-07 Flow-through, wash and strip fractions and the mass balance not recorded {#sec-pd07}

PCP-007 §5.4 required the flow-through, wash and strip fractions to be sampled and a mass balance made for every run, with the strip analysed when the mass balance falls short. No fraction result and no mass balance is in the record, so the strip test could not be triggered. Version 1.0 of this report stated that the flow-through and the wash were assayed, with no result recorded. Where host cell protein is removed within the step, in the load, the wash or the strip, therefore cannot be shown, and the mechanism of @sec-platform is not tested on that point.

### PD-007-08 Packing tests not recorded for each campaign {#sec-pd08}

PCP-007 §5.1 required plate count and asymmetry to be tested, and the column released against SOP-2008, before each campaign. Plate count and asymmetry are recorded for the `{python} N_SD_Q` scale-down runs of the qualification only, with no acceptance limits. No packing result is recorded for the screening, response-surface and flow-rate campaigns. Version 1.0 of this report stated that the column was released, with no result recorded. A change in packing between or within campaigns therefore cannot be excluded from the record.

### PD-007-09 Fractionated runs not in the plan {#sec-pd09}

The study S-CEX-FRC was made and is reported, and it is in neither version of the plan. Its fractionated run collected the eluate in fractions to read the elution profile against the stop collect, and its samples were analysed by SEC and by nrCE-SDS (@sec-analytical). Its results support the method decision for fragments and are not used for any range or class of this step.

### PD-007-10 Approaches where the plan sets no threshold, and step-level capability {#sec-pd10}

PCP-007 §7 and §8 name the evidence for seven decisions but no threshold. This report states and applies its own approach for each (@sec-thresholds). Three of the decisions could not be made as planned, because the packing records, the fractions and the load results are missing (PD-007-08, PD-007-07 and PD-007-05). PCP-007 §5.5 also asked for the capability of the step, from the fitted models over draws within the NOR, as a Cpk for each attribute against its intermediate criterion. Capability is given for the drug substance from the integrated model instead (@sec-capability), which is the estimate PCMP-001 Version 2.0 §7.9 uses.

### PD-007-11 Feed lots not recorded {#sec-pd11}

PCP-007 §6.2 required the feed lot of every run to be recorded and the lots compared where more than one is used. The record does not name the feed lot of any run. A lot effect therefore cannot be separated from the run-order drift of host cell protein or from the scatter between runs.

### PD-007-12 Load/wash buffer named Tris in Version 1.0 {#sec-pd12}

Version 1.0 of this report named the load/wash buffer of lot `{python} LOT['id']`, used in screening run `{python} RUN6`, a Tris buffer (@sec-dev01). The lot is an acetate load/wash buffer. The name in Version 1.0 was a transcription error, found in the Version 2.0 review. The re-test pH of the lot, `{python} f"{dev_007_01_retest_ph:g}"`, lies in the buffering range of acetate. The correction changes no result of this report.
